Chief Complaint: NEPHROLITHIASIS, COMPLEX Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Right PCNL, Right antegrade ureteroscopy, right antegrade ureteral stent, right antegrade nephrostogram HPI: is a delightful woman with a history of multiple sclerosis. She developed an infected obstructing series of stones on the right kidney several months ago and presented to our institution. She was in intensive care and had a right nephrostomy tube placed. She has come to the operating room today for management of residual stones. Hospital Course: Ms. was admitted to urology where she underwent cystoscopy, right antegrade nephrostogram with interpretation, right PCNL for stone greater than 2 cm, right antegrade ureteral stent placement, removal of right nephrostomy tube. She tolerated the procedure well and recovered in the PACU before transfer to the general surgical floor. See the dictated operative note for full details. Overnight, the patient was hydrated with intravenous fluids and received appropriate perioperative prophylactic antibiotics. On POD1, indwelling urethral catheter was left in place. POD1 Ms. was discharged to home with resumption of home services (she has access to RN in her group home) and her pain was well controlled, she was tolerating a regular diet, and afebrile. Patient was explicitly advised to follow up as directed as the indwelling ureteral stent must be removed and or exchanged. Chief Complaint: hypertension urgency, vomiting Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Trach change on . 6.0 Portex Blue-Line cuffed tube HPI: w/HTN, two previous strokes w/residual left sided weakness, nonverbal, trach/peg presenting from nursing home with hypertensive urgency. Per nursing facility pt noted to have BP 218/124 and large volume emesis at yesterday. nitropaste was applied without improvement in BP and pt referred to ED. No recent changes in medications. Per ED report family (son/niece) state 2 days of "not feeling well", multiple episodes of nonbloody emesis and less interactive with them. Family thinks she is having left leg pain but unsure of any injuries that may have occurred. In ED pt with poorly controlled BP as high as 218/119. Head CT without acute infarct. Given 10mg IV Hospital Course: w/HTN, two previous strokes w/residual left sided weakness, nonverbal, s/p trach/PEG presenting from nursing home with hypertensive urgency. Hypertensive Urgency: possibly due to UTI, or lack of clonidine. Patient has previously been admitted with hypertensive urgency, both in setting of infection, inability to tolerate PO and also due to possible inadequate medication administration. Patient has been noted on prior admissions for elevated BP to not have her clonidine patch on. It is possible that she self-removes the patch. On this admission, her renal function was stable, troponin was negative, EKG did not show any ischemic changes compared to baseline and CT head did not show any acute bleed. She was restarted on her home lisinopril and clonidine patch, and also received a 1 time dose of PO clonidine with return of blood pressure to normal parameters. She was also treated for UTI (see below). In the future, if there continues to be concern re: clonidine patch administration, can consider switching to clonidine pills administered via G-tube. Urinary tract infection: Unable to ascertain if patient symptomatic. Chief Complaint: "I feel like I'm losing touch with reality." Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: None HPI: This is a year old single, adopted, Asian woman, originally from , currently full time student at who self-presented to the ED endorsing three weeks of multiple depressive symptoms and suicidal ideation with plan to overdose on alcohol and prescription medication. She states she has been feeling anxious and somewhat depressed ever since starting school at three months ago (was previously in college in . Over the past several weeks, she describes a "confidence crisis" and severe anxiety with intermittent panic attacks which were preventing her from concentrating in her classes and completing her assignments. She began seeing an NP at three weeks ago, who initiated treatment with Lexapro and PRN Ativan. Patient's clinician advised her to discontinue Lexapro last week, in the setting of worsening depression. . In recent weeks, patient states that she has felt worthless, hopeless, guilty, and dreadful of the future. She states that she has been having escalating intrusive thoughts of death. "It's like everywhere I look and everyone I look at, all I see is death." She states she thinks about committing suicide daily and has thought of a plan to obtain alcohol from a friend and overdose Hospital Course: Ms. is a yo Asian female, adopted, single child, college student with a remote history of cutting but no known chronic psychiatric conditions, no prior episodes of suicidality or hospitalizations, who presented with three weeks of worsening depression and suicidality and a plan to overdose on alcohol and prescription medication. . On admission, patient irritable, demanding discharge. She discussed many stressors over the last several months, namely moving to a new place, extreme self-imposed pressure to perform in school, ongoing feelings of failure despite "getting all A's," chronic feelings that she is "less intelligent" than her peers. She also endorsed interpersonal conflict at school (does not like roommate, requesting room change), disagreements with her parents (they are "nice" but she feels like they cannot "grapple with mental illness"). Patient also endorsed increased frequency of panic attacks in the last several weeks which she described as episodes of "doom." She noted regularly only sleeping ~5 hours, cycling patterns of appetite with accompanying weight gain/loss, irritable mood, concern that she "cannot get better" and will always be depressed, as well as near-const PMH: Past Psychiatric History: Hospitalizations: Denies. His blood pressures have normalized and remain stable. Chief Complaint: Obstructing ureteral stone in solitary kidney Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Cystoscopy, ureteral stent placement PMH: of right nephroureterectomy for upper tract UCC in . He had pain return around 4:30pm and went back to the hospital. He was transferred to for further evaluation. At , he endorses pain but no nausea or vomiting. He had not voided for 8+ hours. He was noted on CT to have a distal left ureteral stone in setting of solitary kidney. It was decided he would be admitted and undergo stent placement.

Chief Complaint: SOB and right sided chest pain Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Right pleural pigtail catheter placement HPI: yo M refers sudden onset acute right stabbing pain and difficulty breathing while lifting weights in the gym. He had never experienced this before and came in to the ER for evaluation. His chest xray revealed a large right pneumothorax and a right pleural pigtail catheter was placed and he was admitted to the Thoracic Surgery service. Hospital Course: Mr. was evaluated by the Thoracic Surgery service in the Emergency Room and admitted to the hospital for further management of his right pigtail catheter. The tube was on suction and there was initially an air leak which eventually resolved. His chest xray showed gradual re expansion of the right lung. His pain was controlled with Tylenol and Oxycodone and he was otherwise doing well. His room air saturations were 97%. He underwent a waterseal trial on and his lung remained expanded. The pigtail catheter was removed on and his post pull chest xray revealed a 5 mm right apical space. He continued to have room air saturations of 96-99% and his pain had resolved. He was discharged to home on and will follow up in the Thoracic Clinic in 2 weeks. Chief Complaint: Shortness of breath Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: None HPI: The patient shared that last week he was in with his wife and granddaughter. He notes his granddaughter had a cold during this time. Then about days ago he began to feel congested and develop a cough productive of clear mucous. He also felt cold, but did not take his temperature to check for fevers. His symptoms persisted, and he also began to feel his breathing was wheezy. Because his breathing was not getting better, he came to the ED. In the ED, initial VS were: 98.6 70 158/68 18 90% RA. Exam was notable for "mild respiratory distress." Hospital Course: Mr. is a year old man with history of EtOH cirrhosis with s/p liver transplant in , PVD s/p femoral bypass and MSSA vascular graft infection , CAD s/p PCIx2, who presented to with hypoxia, wheezing, congestion, and cough thought to be due to COPD exacerbation in the setting of recent upper respiratory tract infection. ACUTE PROBLEMS HYPOXIA URI COPD EXACERBATION Pt reported recent onset cough, congestion, rhinorrhea after travel with family. He developed progressive wheezing, dyspnea and productive cough. CXR revealed mild vascular pulmonary congestion. He denied orthopnea, PND. He had mild swelling (L>R). EKG was w/o ischemic changes. He was treated for COPD exacerbation with IV methylprednisolone followed by 40 mg PO prednisone, and azithromycin. We covered for CAP with IV ceftriaxone, although given very low suspcision for CAP, we discontinued this medication on hospital day 3. He was also treated with standing nebulizers. He also received one dose of IV lasix given pulmonary edema. PO lasix was increased upon discharge. He was discharged with prednisone and azithromycin to complete five day course. Congestive heart failure Pulmonary edema swelling Patient notes chronic swelling PMH: - EtOH/HepC cirrhosis c/b HCC s/p ABO-incompatible liver transplant plus splenectomy on tacrolimus -Peripheral vascular disease s/p L-CIA stent , left right fem-femo bypass with right femoral endarterectomy , MSSA infected fem-fem bypass with repair and cutdown MSSA vascular graft infection on chronic dicloxacillin -S/p gastric bypass -CKD stage III -CAD s/p BMS to LAD in and BMS to RCA in -Gout -Squamous cell carcinoma s/p MOHS

Original — ICD: C76.81
Chief Complaint: Abdominal Pain Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Abdominal lymph node biopsy HPI: HIV (CD4 359, VL undetectable on on HAART with no history of AIDS, melanoma (resected), colon polyps, who presents with abdominal pain. For the past two weeks, he has had a diffuse abdominal pain, which he finds hard to fully describe. "Like a rock sitting in my abdomen." He has had some constitutional symptoms. For about two weeks he has had chills. Woke up in a cold sweat on two occasions during this time. Appetite has been poor and he feels like he may have lost some weight unintentionally. Of note, he reports regular negative PPD testing, most recently about years ago and denies any TB exposures. He also has regular colonoscopies; most recently a year ago. He presented to the ED where vitals were stable, and a CT abdomen/pelvis showed diffuse retroperitoneal and L inguinal LAD. His ED providers decided to admit him for expedited workup and coordination of care. On discussion of the case, I expressed that going into the weekend we would also have limited ability to coordinate his care and that expediting his workup would depend largely on the avai Hospital Course: year old man with a history of well controlled HIV (CD4 359, VL undetectable) on ART, melanoma (resected), and colon polyps, who presented with abdominal pain and was found to have diffuse mesenteric and RP lymphadenopathy, admitted for expedited biopsy. The patient felt well on the day of discharge. We were all frustrated by not having a preliminary biopsy result but Heme/Onc agreed it was safe for him to be discharged and they will call him with the result. Abdominal Pain L supraclavicular and axillary, retroperitoneal and mesenteric, and left inguinal lymphadenopathy -noted to have B-symptoms (chills, drenching sweats) -very concerning for malignancy, usual lymphoproliferative disorders seem more likely than HIV-associated lymphoma given excellent viral control, do not have significant suspicion for TB -however, Radiology's read raised abdominal TB as a possible cause. Case was discussed with and ACS, but both services requested TB be ruled out prior to any biopsy. PPD was placed and was negative, and core biopsy was performed (rather than excisional biopsy) to assess for any signs of TB. -LDH and uric acid were elevated so he was started on allopurinol -Heme/Onc was consulted a PMH: HIV Numerous colon polyps Melanoma (resected Hyperlipidemia BPH Dry eye syndrome Macular degeneration Neuropathy Occular rosacea

Chief Complaint: Left Breast Cancer Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: 1) Left mastectomy with left sentinel lymph node biopsy 2) immediate unilateral flap reconstruction HPI: Ms. is a Hispanic woman with biopsy-proven invasive carcinoma of the left breast for which she is planning to undergo skin sparing mastectomy. Ms. is interested in autologous tissue breast reconstruction and presents to discuss surgical options. A genetic workup is pending and this will likely influence the patient to undergo double mastectomy if a genetic mutation is discovered. Hospital Course: Patient taken to the operating room on for immediate left Unilateral . Please refer to the operative report for further detail. Patient tolerated operation without intraoperative complications. Extubated in OR and transferred to PACU. Unilateral flap remained WWP with strong signal and patient transferred to the floor of POD0. Patients postoperative course was uneventful. Patient was transitioned to regular diet as tolerated and switched to PO medications on POD1. Flap continued to have strong Doppler signal and vioptex strength throughout hospital course. Upon discharge patient was tolerating regular diet, passing gas/BM, tolerating PO pain medications and drains were appropriate. Scheduled follow up was made with Dr. . PMH: PSYCHIATRIC HISTORY: She had depression in the setting of her 2 previous pregnancies. First in , pt experienced depression during the pregnancy (depressed mood, some tearfulness) and relates that to the stress of her first pregnancy and financial stress. She took Wort during that time. She then developed post-partum depression after her second baby was born in , again described as depressed mood and at that time was treated with citalopram for 3 months, which she found helpful. The depression then resolved until she found out she was pregnant this time at about 3 weeks. She has never had menta Physical Exam: AVSS General: Well appearing in NAD CV: RRR Pulm: Breathing comfortably on RA Breast: Left breast with abdominal flap WWP. No evidence of erythema, seroma, or hematoma. Incision healing well. Strong dopplerable signal Abd: Soft, NT, ND. Incisions c/d/I. No fluid collections. Chief Complaint: right diabetic foot ulcer Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: ray partial resection ( ) HPI: Mr. is a year old male with a history of DMII, prostate cancer s/p resection, melanoma s/p resection, renal cancer s/p resection who presents with a diabetic right foot ulcer. The notes that he has previously had left foot ulcer requiring inpatient antibiotics. The noted that he has an ulcer on the plantar surface of his foot that he has had for some time. He noted skin breakdown on the lateral aspect of his right small toe after playing golf. This rapidly progressed and he subsequently developed an ulcer with drainage and purulence. The ulcer progressed and the patients toe became progressively darker over subsequent days. The notes that he has had fever and chills with some sinus congestion over the past 2 days, but this has now resolved. the ED: Initial Hospital Course: SUMMARY: Mr. is a man with DMII, prostate cancer s/p resection, melanoma s/p resection, renal cancer s/p resection, who presented to the hospital with a diabetic right foot ulcer. He had distal R ray amputation with redebridement the OR (clean margins) , sent for path and micro. He was treated with vanc, cefepime, and flagyl empirically. Cultures positive for group B strep, MSSA, and pansensitive pseudomonas aeruginosa. He was switched to oral regimen of augmentin and ciprofloxacin prior to discharge for total of 10 day course from operation set to complete . ACTIVE ISSUES: R metatarsal diabetic foot ulcer s/p partial amputation presented with R metatarsal diabetic foot ulcer with gas gangrene noted on foot x-ray. Had partial ray amputation and debridement . Per podiatry, clean bony margins were noted the OR after further debridement, with low concern for any remaining osteomyelitis that required prolonged IV antibiotics. He was treated on broad IV antibiotics including vanc/CTX/flagyl while wound cultures and OR pathology were pending. Cultures from grew mixed bacterial flora including group B strep, MSSA, and pseudomonas aeruginosa. His home course had been uneventful, aside from a fall 2 days ago on his left hip for which he evaluated at urgent care with plain film showing no fracture. This morning, he woke up feeling more lethargic than normal. On pulse oximeter at his group home, he was found to have a desaturation to 89%. The patient denies any shortness of breath, chest pain, fevers, chills, cough, dysuria, or hemoptysis. He reports L sided tenderness. In the ED, initial vitals: 98.0 | 125/44 | 80 | 24 | 92% RA - Exam notable for: Rhonchorous breath sounds in the right lower lobe. Moving all extremities no evidence of trauma. - Hospital Course: SUMMARY STATEMENT with a history of developmental delay, HFrEF (EF 35% , CVA, chronic dysphagia/aspiration, and recent admission for PNA, who presents with lethargy and hypoxia, with rhonchorous lung sounds bilaterally and a CXR with bibasilar effusions most concerning for aspiration pneumonitis. Antibiotics were deescalated, patient improved. Patient was not able to participate in chest physical therapy nor use acapella valve, assessed as physical therapy at his baseline. His hip pain was well controlled with Tylenol and lidocaine patch. He may benefit from additional supervision while eating at his day program to prevent recurrent episodes. Chief Complaint: Thunderclap headaches with MRA HPI: This is a year old healthy man who was referred to ED by his outpatient neurologist for expedited work-up of thunderclap headaches with MRA Hospital Course: Mr. was admitted with MRA with concern for possible vertebrobasilar vasospasm, however the change in caliber of the vertebral artery was immediately after the takeoff of , and could therefore be anatomic. CTA was performed, which showed unchanged vessel caliber change. TCD was performed with normal velocities, indicating less likely vasospasm and more likely normal anatomy. Urine tox positive for cocaine, but Mr. adamantly denies cocaine use, therefore unclear if this may be false positive and may or may not be related to the headaches. His headaches were therefore thought likely due to primary headache syndrome: exercise-induced headache and/or post-coital headache. He was started on propranolol for prophylaxis. He received a 30mg dose of immediate release propranolol prior to discharge, which he tolerated without orthostasis nor drop in BP, and will be discharged with propranolol LA 60mg daily Headache abortive therapy considered, but given severe duration 30 sec and moderate severity duration <10 minutes, this was felt unlikely to be effective. Physical Exam: ADMISSION EXAM: Vitals: T98, RR18, HR89, SBP140/74, SaO2 98 General: Awake, cooperative, NAD. HEENT: NC/AT, no scleral icterus noted, MMM, no lesions noted in oropharynx Neck: Supple, no carotid bruits appreciated. No nuchal rigidity Pulmonary: Lungs CTA bilaterally without R/R/W Cardiac: RRR, nl. S1S2, no M/R/G noted Abdomen: soft, NT/ND, normoactive bowel sounds, no masses or organomegaly noted. Extremities: No edema. Skin: no rashes or lesions noted. Neurologic: -Mental Status: Alert, oriented x 3. Able to relate history without difficulty. Attentive, able to name backward without difficult

Original — ICD: S72.101
Chief Complaint: Right distal femur fracture Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: ORIF Right distal femur fracture on (Dr. . HPI: F with MS, wheelchair bound at baseline, presents with R distal femur fracture s/p mechanical fall. She was transferring from wheelchair to lift when she had insufficient support from her aide and fell, with immediate cracking sensation and pain in the right thigh. She denies pain elsewhere. She is unable to ambulate at baseline secondary to MS and does not use her legs for transfers. Hospital Course: The patient presented to the emergency department and was evaluated by the orthopedic surgery team. The patient was found to have right distal femur fracture and was admitted to the orthopedic surgery service. The patient was taken to the operating room on for ORIF, which the patient tolerated well. For full details of the procedure please see the separately dictated operative report. The patient was taken from the OR to the PACU in stable condition and after satisfactory recovery from anesthesia was transferred to the floor. The patient was initially given IV fluids and IV pain medications, and progressed to a regular diet and oral medications by POD 1. The patient was given antibiotics and anticoagulation per routine. The patient's home medications were continued throughout this hospitalization. The patient worked with who determined that discharge to rehab was appropriate. The hospital course was otherwise unremarkable. Geriatrics was consulted for assistance in management and a urine culture was negative for UTI. At the time of discharge the patient's pain was well controlled with oral medications, incisions were clean/dry/intact, and the patient was voiding/moving bowels spont PMH: Complete heart block, S/P DDD pacemaker. Pacer placed . Most recently interrogated Diabetes mellitus. Hypothyroidism. Multiple sclerosis. Obesity. Chronic lower extremity edema with venous insufficiency. Chronic urinary tract infection due to indwelling Foley catheter. Uterine polyps and history of uterine bleed.

Chief Complaint: "My friend brought me to the emergency room." Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: None HPI: For further details of the history and presentation, please see OMR including Dr. initial consultation note dated . . Briefly, this is a single female to male transgendered man, self-reported history of depression, anxiety, no prior psychiatric hospitalizations, history of self-injurious behaviors, who self presented to with a friend with worsening depressive symptoms and suicidal ideation with intent to overdose on pills in the setting of numerous psychosocial stressors. . Upon initial interview in the emergency department, patient reported that on the day of presentation on the floor with his room with large number of pills laid out in front of him. He reported he had been researching on how many pills he needed to take in order to make sure he killed himself prior to his friend, , finding him. The patient stated he had Lexapro, Adderall, and Co-codamol, some of these prescriptions which were prescribed with Zofran. The patient was apparently able to take his medications when his friend came to the room and stopped the patient. reported that he had only gone to the patient's room after receiving a number of frantic phone calls and text messages from the patient's, stating he need Hospital Course: Mr. is a yo F to M transgender individual c h/o unspecified depressive d/o who self-presented at the behest of her friend after she was found counting/collecting pills c intent to OD in the context of worsening depressed mood. On interviews, patient endorsed depressed mood, anhedonia, multiple neurovegetative symptoms and suicidal ideation all in the context of psychosocial stressors like poor school performance and difficulty c gender transition given parent's reported limited understanding. MSE is notable for dysphoric affect congruent c mood. Constellation of findings is consistent c MDD; however, persistent depressive d/o +/- a superimposed major depressive episode or adjustment d/o remain on the differential as well. Additionally, gender dysphoria and stressors relating to her transition in social context are contributing factors. . . Safety/Legal: CV signed/accepted on admission, and patient placed on q15 min checks, green Sharps and unit restriction and remained there for the duration of her hospitalization. Patient did not engage in any unsafe behaviors and did not require physical, mechanical or chemical restraints. Psych . Major Depressive Disorder: on initial presentatio PMH: Past psychiatric history: - Diagnoses: unclear but with symptoms of depression and anxiety - SA/SIB: denies history of prior suicide attempts, history of self injury including banging head, hitting hands against a tree, holding stuff until it cuts the inside of hand, breaking off nails - Hospitalizations: denies - Therapist: seeing for years - Psychiatrist: Unclear, sees a practitioner at - Trials: Lexapro .

Chief Complaint: fevers, cough, abdominal pain Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: None HPI: POD2 from , BSO, vault suspension, anterior repair, sub-urethral sling, and cystoscopy c/b bladder perforation who presents to the ED with fevers, suprapubic pain, dysuria, and cough. Patient reports pain started earlier today with associated dysuria, increased urinary frequency, and straining to void. No hematuria. She had associated nausea at the time with fevers and chills that progressed later in the day. She was taking acetaminophen at home for pain with no improvement. She denies any dizziness, chest pain, or shortness or breath. She has mild vaginal spotting, no abnormal discharge. ROS: all systems reviewed and negative unless mentioned above Hospital Course: Ms. is a year old woman who presented on POD 2 from a , BSO, vault suspension, anterior repair, sub-urethral sling, cystoscopy for pelvic organ prolapse and stress urinary incontinence with fevers, cough, and abdominal pain. Her initial exam was notable for a T max of F, tachycardia to 115, ronchi over the right lower lung field, and tenderness to palpation in the suprpubic and right lower quadrant without rebound or guarding. Her WBC and lactate were within normal limits, and a urinalysis was also normal. Still, given her immunocompromised state, urine and blood cultures were ordered (urine no growth; blood pending). A chest X Ray showed a right middle lobe consolidation, which was confirmed on CT. CT abdomen and pelvis also demonstrated a 2.8 x 3.8 phlegmon without a drainable fluid collection. The foley that was place in the ED out of concern for retention was removed on hospital day 2 after she passed a trial of void cc in, 150 cc out). Based on these findings she was diagnosed with an aspiration pneumonia with low concern for intrabdominal/post-surgical infection. She was started on Ceftriaxone/cipro/flagyl on and, as her condition improved, narrowed to unasyn on and then augm Physical Exam: Vitals: 98.0, BP 150 / 65, HR 73, RR 18, SpO2 97% RA General: alert and oriented x3, no acute distress Cardiovascular: regular rate and rhythm, normal s1 and s2, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops Pulmonary: normal work of breathing, left lung field is cta, right lung has fine crackles at base to mid-lung field (improved since yesterday) Abdominal: normal active bowel sounds, soft, non-distended, mildly tender to palpation in the suprapubic area, no masses palpated Extremities: warm and well perfused, no calf tenderness, no edema, pneumoboots on Pertinent Results: 08:20AM WBC-8.5 RBC-2.99 HGB-9.6 HC

She went to Urgent Care on where she says they performed an extensive workup including CXR, flu swab, CT scan, nasopharyngeal endoscopy as well as possibly EGD. She was told initially that her throat was inflamed but when they looked with a camera they found no evidence of airway obstruction or any abnormalities. Her breathing started to improve with breathing treatments and they wanted to keep observing her that evening but she preferred to be discharged AMA. She was discharged with a course of Levaquin. She notes she has an inhaler that she uses rarely which was prescribed by her PCP while ago for DOE but nothing as severe as her current symptoms. Chief Complaint: shortness of breath Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: none HPI: hx of asthma who is presenting with wheezing and SOB following a week of fever, cough, and body aches. Patient states that symptoms first started on with runny nose, fever, and body aches. On , patient presented to PCP with these symptoms. Had been improving, but that morning had experienced worsening chest tightness, like a "elephant was sitting on my chest." Patient was prescribed azithromycin and prednisone by PCP. She initially felt that she was improving, though she continued to cough up some sputum, especially at night. On , she began to feel worse again, as though she could "hardly breathe". She was seen in clinic on , and was sent for a chest x-ray. The following day she did not feel that she was significantly improved, and she presented to the ED. This is the patient's fourth documented asthma exacerbation this year. In , patient presented to ED with asthma. Was hospitalized in with asthma exacerbation. She was treated with prednisone and nebulizers, and was started on Singulair prior to discharge. However, records indicate that the last time she filled this medication was in , and patient currently reports that she never took it. At that time, discharge peak flow 240. She Hospital Course: hx of asthma who is presenting with wheezing and SOB following a week of cold-like symptoms. Asthma: Patient with a history of asthma and presentation consistent with asthma exacerbation in setting of viral illness. On arrival to the ED, patient was started on nebulizer treatments. A flu swab was negative. A chest x-ray showed an opacity, mostly likely atelectasis. The patient's prednisone taper, which had been started in the outpatient setting on was continued. Azithromycin was stopped (no current infectious symptoms, no clear infiltrate on CXR, and not indicated for asthma exacerbation). On her last hospitalization, she had been started on singulair 10mg daily. However, she had not been taking this at home. This was restarted. She was continued on her fluticasone-salmeterol inhaler, as well as albuterol and ipratropium nebulizers. She was discharged w/plan to follow up with Allergy clinic for consideration of starting Xolair. Hypertension: On admission, patient noted to be hypertensive to 221/101, which improved without intervention. This had also been noted on previous admission in , thought to be secondary to steroids. Her pressures then remained in the 130s-150s/50s for the re PMH: - Asthma - Hyperlipidemia - Obesity - Chronic LBP - GERD - Hiatal Hernia - Trigeminal Neuralgia - Hemorrhoids - Sciatica - Allergic Rhinitis - Fatty Liver - patient told this many years ago, with no active workup - Pulmonary Nodules - multiple stable pulmonary nodules first noted . Chief Complaint: Left tibial plateau fracture Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: ORIF Left lateral tibial plateau fracture Hospital Course: The patient presented to the emergency department and was evaluated by the orthopedic surgery team. The patient was found to have left lateral tibial plateau fracture and was admitted to the orthopedic surgery service. The patient was taken to the operating room on for ORIF of tibial plateau fracture, which the patient tolerated well. For full details of the procedure please see the separately dictated operative report. The patient was taken from the OR to the PACU in stable condition and after satisfactory recovery from anesthesia was transferred to the floor. The patient was initially given IV fluids and IV pain medications, and progressed to a regular diet and oral medications by POD 1. The patient was given antibiotics and anticoagulation per routine. The patient's home medications were continued throughout this hospitalization. The patient worked with who determined that discharge to home was appropriate. The hospital course was otherwise unremarkable. At the time of discharge the patient's pain was well controlled with oral medications, incisions were clean/dry/intact, and the patient was voiding/moving bowels spontaneously. The patient is WBAT in unlocked brace in the left l PMH: 1. Lactose intolerance. 2. Questionable heart murmur in childhood, seemingly resolved. 3. Asthma. 4. Hypercholesterolemia, resolved. 5. History of fatty liver. 6. History of elevated hemoglobin A1c, resolved. 7. History of ovarian cyst. 8. History of menorrhagia. 9. Plantar fasciitis, resolved. Past Surgical History: Laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy in . Physical Exam: AVSS NAD, A&Ox3 RLE: Incisions well approximated. Mild edema. Mild ecchymoses. Fires . Original — ICD: M32.9
Chief Complaint: Chest Pain Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: None HPI: In brief, this patient is a y/o F w/SLE c/b membranous glomerulonephritis who presents for evaluation of chest pain and fevers. Patient was recently diagnosed with SLE, and she has been following with Dr. as an outpatient. Over the past month, patient has had high fevers, which progressively became higher and increased in frequency. This was also associated with joint pains, night sweats, and weight loss. She was started on CellCept and prednisone 30mg PO QDay last , and her fevers resolved. In addition, her joint pains improved significantly. With regards to her SLE, she notes occasional rashes on her arms. No head rashes or ulcers. She has had some alopecia. On the night prior to admission, patient developed chest pain, worse with movement. She describes dull chest pain, without associated light-headedness or dizziness. Pain is worse with changing positions, but is particularly bad when she lies flat or on her left side. She also reports a dry cough for a month, which is currently worse than prior. On the day of presentation, she started having fevers again, as high as 104. She also notes new left elbow pain. ROS otherwise negative for n/v, bleeding, easy bruising, melena/hematoc Hospital Course: is a w/SLE c/b membranous glomerulonephritis who presented for evaluation of chest pain and fevers most likely SLE flare. Lupus Flare: The patient's fevers and chest pain were both attributed to a flare of her SLE as both resolved with methylprednisolone and without antibiotics. For infectious workup blood cultures were drawn and showed no growth, urine cultures grew mixed flora consistent with skin contamination, lyme serologies, anaplasma and babesia all came back negative. Four serial troponins were drawn and were all <0.01, making ACS an unlikely cause of her chest pain. Her elevated CRP (163.2), low C3 and C4 (73, 4 respectively) were also consistent with a lupus flare. Rheumatology was consulted and she was treated with 3 days of IV methylprednisolone 1000mg qday. She was also continued on cellcept and started on atovaquone for PCP . After completing the methylprednisolone her symptoms resolved, so she was discharged home on 60mg prednisone QDAY and instructed to follow-up with rheumatology as an outpatient. Anemia. The patient was found to be anemic so iron PMH: auto-immune lupus like condition glomerulonephritis submucous leiomyoma of uterus s/p abdominal myomectomy Appendectomy Tonsillectomy R and L arthoroscopic knee surgery L carpel tunnel release

Chief Complaint: RUE pain/weakness Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: none HPI: Mr. is a man with afib on apixaban, CHF, and LBBB who presents from clinic for evaluation of left hand pain and right arm pain. History was obtained with help from a in Yesterday, he developed acute onset numbness and pain in his right hand. Started at 2pm when he was on the bus going home after working for a day. Did not do anything out of the ordinary at work, did not lift heavy boxes. Pain (numbness, some tingling with needle-like sensation) was most severe in his right thumb, and it went up his right arm gradually. Felt like his arm was not there, and he would have to use his left hand to move his right arm around. At , sensation was returning, and he started being able to move his arm again. He took eliquis at 8pm, then another at 10pm, and another at midnight. He felt like this helped his weakness. He went to work today and noticed that he was unable to do things as quickly with his right hand. He was also having some trouble with fine motor movements such as buttoning his pants. Still has pain in her right thumb and thenar eminence, sometimes his fingertips as well. Pain is worse with certain positions. Of note, he has been taking 2 tablets of eliquis at midnight since start Hospital Course: man with afib on AC (but not taking it correctly at the moment) presents with R hand pain with a report of weakness after sleeping on the arm. He has had weakness of the arm in the past after sleeping on it in a peculiar way. He main complaint that brought him into the hospital is pain in the joints of the hand. Xray confirmed severe arthritis in the first CMC and triscaphe joint. He was prescribed ibuprofen for pain and given a prescription for a wrist splint to stabilize his hand while sleeping. He was also instructed to take his Eliquis BID in order to best prevent future strokes. He should follow up with his PCP in one week.

Chief Complaint: Dyspnea Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: None HPI: BIBA from home for worsening dyspnea x1 week, adm COPD exacerbation. Patient is speaking but refused translator in ED, wished to speak through his significant other. Has had dyspnea for the past week, was seen at last week and started on Ventolin. After being put in the ambulance, he received a DuoNeb and Albuterol Neb with improvement in his symptoms. He had URI sx with rhinnorhea before his cough began; initially it was nonproductive, became productive in the last day. He's had subjective fevers. Denies CP, n/v. He endorses orthopnea and bloating, denied leg swelling. He had R shoulder pain. He does have a pack year smoking history, stopped years ago. In the ED, initial VS were: 98.6 102 149/78 28 99% RA. ED Hospital Course: M presented with worsening dyspnea, admitted for hypoxemia & presumed COPD exacerbation. Hypoxemia/Dyspnea: Sinusitis: Differential included asthma/reactive airways disease (though patient has no history of this) or COPD (though his smoking history is very brief, and he is relatively young); a flare of either could have been triggered by URI with his acute sinusitis. He was treated with DuoNebs, albuterol PRN, prednisone and azithromycin with rapid improvement. He will completed 5 days of azithromycin/prednisone as an outpatient, and was also discharged on Spiriva and albuterol prn to follow-up with his PCP. For his sinusitis, he was given fluticasone nasal spray. : Elevated Lactate: Likely pre-renal/poor PO intake, resolved with IVF and treatment of his respiratory issues as above. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: - Patient to complete total 5 days of prednisone/azithromycin - Patient prescribed tiotroprium and albuterol prn - Likely trigger is patient's sinusitis/rhinitis, for which he was prescribed a steroid nasal spray - Patient may benefit from PFTs/pulmonary outpatient consultation given his relatively brief smoking history and young age for COPD - Patient describes bloating with meals, Physical Exam: was recorded as: On NC O2 Diffuse wheezes and ronchi ED

Chief Complaint: Right hip pain Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Right total hip arthroplasty HPI: year old male with right hip OA refractory to cortisone injections presents today for total hip arthroplasty. Hospital Course: The patient was admitted to the orthopedic surgery service and was taken to the operating room for above described procedure. Please see separately dictated operative report for details. The surgery was uncomplicated and the patient tolerated the procedure well. Patient received perioperative IV antibiotics. Postoperative course was unremarkable. Otherwise, pain was controlled with a combination of IV and oral pain medications. The patient received lovenox for DVT prophylaxis starting on the morning of POD 1. The foley was removed and the patient was voiding independently thereafter. The surgical dressing was changed and the Silverlon dressing was removed on POD 2. The surgical incision was found to be clean and intact without erythema or abnormal drainage. The patient was seen daily by physical therapy. Physical Exam: Discharge PE: Well appearing in no acute distress Afebrile with stable

Original — ICD: M72.11
Chief Complaint: Left shoulder pain Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Left reverse total shoulder arthroplasty HPI: Ms. is an year-old right hand dominant woman with a long-standing history of left sided shoulder pain and disability. Having failed conservative modalities including serial corticosteroid injections, it was her preference to proceed with a left reverse total shoulder arthroplasty on . Hospital Course: The patient was admitted to the Orthopaedic Sports Medicine Service for advanced rotator cuff arthropathy. The patient was taken to the OR and underwent a left reverse total shoulder arthroplasty . Please see operative report for full details. The patient tolerated the procedure without difficulty and was transferred to the PACU in stable condition, and then transferred to the floor in the usual fashion. Postoperatively, pain was controlled with an interscalene nerve block, with transition to oral pain medication as tolerated. Perioperative antibiotics and Aspirin for DVT prophylaxis were given as per routine. Diet was advanced without complication and the patient made steady progress. The hospitalization has otherwise been uneventful and the patient has done well. Repeat plain films of the left humerus with two views demonstrated no evidence of fracture. Overnight, patient was noted to have low blood pressure while sleeping. Hct 30. She received a fluid bolus and remained asymptomatic. At discharge, PMH: 1. Stage IIIA NSCLC 2. Dyslipidemia 3. COPD 4. Asthma Physical Exam: Afebrile Vitals stable Left shoulder dressing is clean and dry She is intact distally with + APB/EPL/ADQ The fingers are warm to touch with good capillary refill She has a 2+ radial pulse symmetric to that of the right upper extremity

Chief Complaint: left hip OA Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: left hip replacement , Hospital Course: The patient was admitted to the orthopedic surgery service and was taken to the operating room for above described procedure. Please see separately dictated operative report for details. The surgery was uncomplicated and the patient tolerated the procedure well. Patient received perioperative IV antibiotics. Postoperative course was remarkable for the following: POD 0, patient reported inadequate pain control and Oxycodone was increased to 15mg q4 PRN. POD 1, the patient's hematocrit was 23.5 and she was transfused with one unit of blood. Her post-transfusion hematocrit was 26. Her pain was still an issue, therefore her duration between doses of Oxycodone was decreased from 4 to 3 hours. Patient reported persistent calf pain in operative extremity and an ultrasound was obtained. Results showed no evidence of a DVT. POD 2, patient had complaint of nausea, SOB and chest pain in the AM. She reports ongoing intermittent symptoms since prior to surgery and post-operatively. She attributed symptoms prior to surgery as related to anxiety. An EKG was obtained, which results showed NSR, HR . Patient was given home dose Xanax as requested. Chemistry panel and troponins were obtained. Troponi PMH: - Coronary artery disease - diagnosed on stress test, medically managed - chronic dry mouth: neg eval for Sjogrens - possible PMR previously on chronic corticosteroids - Obstructive Sleep Apnea refusing CPAP - Chronic Lower Back Pain / Sciatica status-post multiple back surgeries - Left Patellar Avulsion Fracture - Osteoarthritis - Osteopenia - Bipolar Disorder / Depression-recently tapered off lithium - questionable MS diagnosis, not corroborated on extensive testing at , no longer on copaxone - Chronic Abdominal Pain s/p multiple abdominal surgeries - Cholecystectomy - Hysterectomy Physical Exam: Well appearing in no acute distress Afebrile with stable

Chief Complaint: vertigo Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: None HPI: is an year old woman with a history of HTN, HLD, DMII, spinal stenosis, hypothyroidism, osteoporosis, BPPV who presents with acute onset vertigo. Patient provides history with the assistance of translator over the phone. Patient states that yesterday at 2200 she acutely felt dizzy, associated with nausea and vomiting. She has experienced similar symptoms previously, most recently years ago. When she has had these symptoms previously, she took meclizine and it resolved the symptoms; she has also been seen by ENT and told that this was an inner ear issue. She took meclizine last night at symptom onset but this did not help. Her symptoms continued, but when she woke up this AM all the dizziness persisted. When asked to describe the dizziness to determine if it is different from lightheadedness, it is difficult for her to say. Interestingly, in the language the word for dizzy encompasses both room spinning and lightheadedness. In any event, she did say that she is experiencing the sensation of abnormal movement around her. She also continues to feel nauseous, though is helping. She also endorses pain at the back of the neck that has started while she is in the ED, she describes this as Hospital Course: is an year old woman with a history of HTN, HLD, DMII, spinal stenosis, hypothyroidism, osteoporosis, BPPV who presents with acute onset vertigo and found to have multiple meningiomas on PMH: RBBB, dyslipid, HTN, DMII, COPD, dyspnea, chronic LBP, hypothyroid s/p lobectomy for CA, reflux, h/o UTI, glaucoma. Chief Complaint: Left hip pain Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Left trochanteric fixation nail HPI: is a female with hx of diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia status post unwitnessed fall at home earlier today. The daughter was worried after she did not initially picked up the phone and she was eventually found down inside her bedroom. She reports she was turning around and subsequently had a fall. She denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, lightheadedness Mealy before the fall. She denies head strike or LOC. Hospital Course: The patient presented to the emergency department and was evaluated by the orthopedic surgery team. The patient was found to have left intertrochanteric femur fracture and was admitted to the orthopedic surgery service. The patient was taken to the operating room on for left trochanteric fixation nail, which the patient tolerated well. For full details of the procedure please see the separately dictated operative report. The patient was taken from the OR to the PACU in stable condition and after satisfactory recovery from anesthesia was transferred to the floor. The patient was initially given IV fluids and IV pain medications, and progressed to a regular diet and oral medications by POD 1. The patient was given antibiotics and anticoagulation per routine. The patient's home medications were continued throughout this hospitalization. The patient worked with who determined that discharge to rehab was appropriate. Chief Complaint: Planned admission for LTM Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: None HPI: Mrs. is a year-old right-handed woman with epilepsy traumatic brain injury who presents for evaluation of her seizure locus in preparation for surgical planning. In just prior to starting , she suffered a traumatic brain injury during a motor vehicle accident. She is not able to recollect the specific events immediately following the collision, but she reportedly experienced a generalized tonic-clonic seizure during her assessment in the ED. She remained in a coma for 1 week following the accident and also required surgery for a broken left humerus. No neurosurgical procedures were performed. During the years following the MVA, she began experiencing heart palpitations, chest pain, migraines, and difficulty sleeping at night. She would occasionally wake up around 3am screaming and drenched in sweat, at which point she would confusedly walk to crew practice, which started much later in the morning. She also noticed a mild decline in her memory and ability to concentrate on and complete her coursework. Over time, her "moments" evolved, and she would feel a sensation travel up through her chest during periods of activity in the daytime. She would then focus on her breathing and slow h Hospital Course: Ms. was admitted to the epilepsy service as above for planned phase I LTM for seizure localization. . The night of admission, she was continued on home doses of AEDs. She had one event characterized as rising sensation which was accompanied by focal delta slowing in the left temporal lobe on EEG, with no clear epileptiform features. We downtitrated her off of both Keppra and Aptiom over several days and she underwent sleep deprivation. . On AM, the morning after her second trial of sleep deprivation, she had an around 3 minute long seizure beginning with lip smacking, blinking, right head version, with tonic extension of arms and legs followed by clonic movements of all four extremities. Post-ictally, there was minimal obvious confusion but the patient was amnestic to the event. From correlation from EEG, this was likely originating from L temporal region. . Per EEG had another electroclinical seizure overnight on t this point, she was restarted on 2000mg Keppra XR on , which was uptitrated to her full dose of 3750mg on while continuing EEG monitoring. She was started on zonisamide 100mg QHS on , and her uptitration plan is listed below. . Zonisamide uptitration plan: Start 100mg Q PMH: head trauma, migraine headache, epilepsy, miscarriage Physical Exam: ADMISSION EXAM: General: Awake, cooperative, NAD. HEENT: NC/AT Pulmonary: CTABL. No R/R/W Cardiac: RRR, nl. S1S2, no M/R/G Abdomen: soft, NT/ND, +BS, no masses or organomegaly noted. Extremities: No C/C/E bilaterally Skin: no rashes or lesions noted. Neurologic: -Mental Status: Alert, oriented x 3. Able to relate history without difficulty. Attentive. Language is fluent with intact repetition and comprehensio

Chief Complaint: Low back pain and radiculopathy Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: : L3-L5 laminectomy and non-instrumented fusion HPI: female with back pain, radiculopathy and lumbar stenosis presents for elective L3-L5 laminectomy and non-instrumented fusion Hospital Course: yo female with back pain, radiculopathy and lumbar stenosis presents for elective L3-L5 laminectomy and non-instrumented fusion. The procedure was uncomplicated. Please see OMR for separately dictated operative report by Dr. . A JP drain was placed. The patient tolerated the procedure well and extubated in the OR. The patient transferred to the PACU for recovery where she remained hemodynamically and neurologically stable. She transferred to the floor for ongoing care. A TLSO brace was ordered and the patient's foley was discontinued. She was tolerating a PO diet and voiding without difficulty. JP drain was removed on POD2. Post op xrays showed no residual drain and expected post-op changes. Patient was fitted for TLSO brace and instructed to wear it at all times out of bed, may use bathroom overnight without brace. and OT saw the patient and recommended home with services. The patient was discharged home with instructions to hold home coumadin for afib for 1 week after surgery. PMH: Factor V Asthma Osteoarthritis Hypertension Phlebitis Hyperlipidemia H. Pylori

Chief Complaint: right homonymous hemianopsia Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Cerebral angiogram Hospital Course: Ms. is a year old otherwise healthy woman who was evaluated at an outside hospital after several days of headaches, occasional "blurry" vision, and a few episodes of confusion. She was found to have a right posterior convexity meningioma as well as a sagittal venous sinus thrombosis, prompting transfer to . Her exam was notable for word finding difficulties as well as a right homonymous hemianopsia which was worse in the inferior as compared to the superior regions. She was initially admitted to the NeuroICU for close monitoring, but was transferred to the Neurology service shortly thereafter. IV heparin was started for anticoagulation. She was evaluated by neurosurgery who recommended against immediate surgical intervention for the meningioma; they will plan to see her in one month to discuss surgical intervention. She underwent a cerebral angiography which redemonstrated her sinus thrombosis in the superior sagittal and bilateral transverse sinuses. MRI brain showed a likely venous infarct in the left occipital lobe, which is likely to explain her visual field deficit. During admission, her aphasia resolved and her hemianopsia improved, though she still as a slight right visual f PMH: x significant for HLD and asthma presented to from with superior sagittal sinus thrombosis in the setting of recently diagnosed right parietal meningioma. Two weeks ago, the patient reported feeling itchy after swimming. She presented to her primary care doctor who started her on an empiric course of oral prednisone. While on the prednisone, she reports bifrontal headaches, which were more severe and different than her previously headaches she has had in the past. After she completed the oral prednisone taper, she became very fatigued. She states that she had persistent headaches at this time. Original — ICD: K52.1
Chief Complaint: Elevated LFT's Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: None HPI: Mrs. is a lady with a history of preeclampsia who presented today to liver clinic with Dr. evaluation of abnormal liver chemistry tests and jaundice on , being directly admitted following liver biopsy today due to worsening jaundice and concern for possible autoimmune hepatitis. The patient was seen in Liver clinic on given her history of abnormal liver chemistries. She was initially found to have elevated LFTs (ALT 716, AST 575)on in the setting of hypertension and preeclampsia requiring her to deliver early. During the clinic visit on , she reported two weeks of fatigue and nausea. Hospital Course: Mrs. is a female with a history of preeclampsia who presented from clinic following liver biopsy due to worsening liver tests and jaundice, concerning for possible autoimmune hepatitis. ACTIVE PROBLEMS: Autoimmune Hepatitis The patient was first found to have elevated liver enzymes in near the end of her pregnancy. She then developed two weeks of nausea/vomiting and presented to liver clinic for follow-up. Her initial workup revealed AST 1518, ALT 2378, Tbili 4.9, positive (1:320) and positive anti-smooth muscle (1:40), which raised the suspicion of autoimmune hepatitis (AIH). Viral serologies were overall unrevealing and RUQ was normal. She underwent a liver biopsy on and was admitted given her persistently elevated AST/ALT and rising Tbili up to 6.2. On , the liver biopsy returned with findings consistent with autoimmune hepatitis. She was given prednisone 60 mg once and discharged with plan to continue prednisone 60 mg and follow-up with Dr. . CBV, CMV and dsDNA were pending at discharge. H/o pre-eclampsia/HTN: History of preeclampsia requiring her to deliver early, back in . Continued on home

Original — ICD: K50.61
Chief Complaint: Abdominal Pain Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: None HPI: w/ Crohn's disease who was sent in by his gastroenterologist (in office w/ presumed Crohn's flare inadequately responsive to PO prednisone. The patient has had increase in his chronic abdominal pain and reports about 12 modestly bloody bowel movements per day. This started in late and was not very responsive to an oral prednisone taper. The patient tells me that the symptoms did not fully resolve, but then worsened again recently a few weeks ago. He started having nausea and intermittent blood-streaked vomiting. He returned to see his gastroenterologist who tried another prednisone taper (started . The patient's n/v resolved, but the gastroenterologist reportedly feels he has had an inadequate response and feels he needs inpatient management and IV steroids. The patient has also been on Entyvio and got an infusion about ten days ago. The patient gives a variable history of whether there have been interruptions in his treatment. Per ED notes, he stopped getting his infusions because of insurance and scheduling issues and had been off treatment for the last year. Conversely, he tells me he started it six months ago and has been getting it every eight weeks. Vitals in the ED were: 98. Hospital Course: is a with history CD dx years ago involving his small bowel and colon currently on Vedolizumab and Predisone presenting with frequent bouts of hematochezia consistent with a flare. Patient has failed multiple prior therapies including 5ASA, Azathioprine, Humira and Remicade, and currently not responding to outpatient therapy. Unclear if having benefit with Vedolizumab, especially with the 14 week gap prior to most recent dosing (usu 8 weeks). CT with evidence of TI and sigmoid/descending colon inflammation, CRP ~45. The GI service recommended 72 hours of IV methylprednisone, possibly checking Vedo levels, and consideration of switching to Stelara as an outpatient. The patient did not wish to remain in house for IV steroids and chose to leave the hospital AMA on despite the urging of the primary team and the GI team. As a contingency he was discharged with a Prednisone burst of 60mg PO daily with plans to see his GI physician in the week of . > 30 minutes spent on discharge care, coordination, and planning. Physical Exam: VITALS: Afebrile and other vitals stable on discharge. CONSTITUTIONAL: well-developed young man in NAD EYE: sclerae anicteric, EOMI ENT: audition grossly intact, MMM, OP clear LYMPHATIC: No LAD CARDIAC: RRR, no M/R/G, JVP not elevated, no edema PULM: normal effort of breathing, LCAB GI: soft, ND, NABS. Marked tenderness to palpation sparing only the LUQ. No bebound or involuntary guarding. GU: no CVA tenderness, suprapubic region soft and nontender MSK: no visible joint effusions or acute deformities. DERM: no visible rash. No jaundice. NEURO: AAOx3. No facial droop, moving all extremities. PS

He recalls getting in to an argument with his mom at that time surrounding his care with his psychiatrist and subsequently not feeling well. Unable to specify any symptoms but "felt off". States he knows when he goes in to DKA but is unable to identify it until someone asks him. Reports not taking his insulin since morning, both long acting and short acting. The reason for this is the injections cause him abdominal and thigh pain and so he avoids same. He does report ongoing benzodiazepine use, with his last dose being AM. Can take anywhere from of alprazolam daily, which he obtains from the street predominantly, although having a prescription for same. He would like to stop taking benzodiazepines but feels he is reliant on them. Does report history of withdrawal seizures in the past. Original — ICD: S72.201
Chief Complaint: Left hip pain Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Surgical fixation, left hip, dynamic hip screw HPI: Ms. is an with history of HTN, HLD & h/o traumatic ICH this past , ambulatory with walker since that fall, who sustained a ground-level mechanical fall on the date prior to presentation in front of her home while walking w/o the walker. She denied HS or LOC. She was taken to ED for further evaluation. In ED, she endorsed left hip pain but denies paresthesias or sensory deficits. She denied injuries elsewhere. At baseline, she lives by herself and is independent of all ADLs. She walks comfortably and is stable using a walker over the past year after her traumatic ICH. The son states that the ICH was managed conservatively with observation (does not recall specifics), and she has no residual deficits from the ICH other than using a walker for stability. She denied antecendent left hip pain. Hospital Course: The patient presented to the emergency department and was evaluated by the orthopedic surgery team. The patient was found to have a left intertrochanteric hip fracture and was admitted to the orthopedic surgery service. The patient was taken to the operating room on for surgical fixation with a dynamic hip screw, which the patient tolerated well. For full details of the procedure please see the separately dictated operative report. The patient was taken from the OR to the PACU in stable condition and after satisfactory recovery from anesthesia was transferred to the floor. The patient was initially given IV fluids and IV pain medications, and progressed to a regular diet and oral medications by POD 1. The patient was given antibiotics and anticoagulation per routine. The patient's home medications were continued throughout this hospitalization. The patient worked with who determined that discharge to rehab was appropriate. The hospital course was otherwise unremarkable. At the time of discharge the patient's pain was well controlled with oral medications, incisions were clean/dry/intact, and the patient was voiding/moving bowels spontaneously. The patient is weight-bearing as toler

Chief Complaint: "I've heard detoxing is the most awful thing in the world" Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: n/a HPI: is a year old woman with a history of depression, anxiety, fibromyalgia, irritable bowel syndrome, osteoarthritis, chronic fatigue syndrome and self-reported history of microscopic colitis who presented to the ED from her PCP's office for assessment of medication abuse and depressed mood. On initial interview on the unit the patient reports intense fear regarding withdrawing from opioids and benzodiazepines. She spoke at length about "horror stories" she has heard about the process and quoted song lyrics describing "the agony" she worries she would go through. She was modestly redirectable but very concerned with somatic complaints including pain in multiple joints and nausea. The patient notes that over the past few weeks she has been feeling increasingly anxious and depressed. She has been using more of her prescribed medications (including oxycodone) than prescribed but states that she does not misuse these medications since she is using "as much as [she needs]." She continues to report desire to stop taking both benzodiazepines and opioids but is not sure she will be able to go through withdrawal without significant assistance from medications. In the ED she reported recent his Hospital Course: is a year old woman with a history of Fibromyalgia, Osteoarthritis, and Irritable Bowel Syndrome who presented ot the ED from her PCP's office for an evaluation of medication misuse and depressed mood. On initial interview the patient reports difficulty caring for herself due to multiple medical problems and severe fatigue. She reports depressed mood, feeling of hopelessness, guilt and amotivation, but no SI. These symptoms have occurred in the setting of multiple psychosocial stressors and have led the patient to use higher then prescribed doses of oxycodone and other medications. The patient is motivated to discontinue use of both opioids and benzodiazepines though is very apprehensive to undergo detox as she worries she will not be able to bear the symptoms. Much of her time on the unit was focused on her many somatic complaint. Chief Complaint: weakness, hypercalcemia Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: NONE HPI: with relapsed refractory multiple myeloma s/p autologous transplant ( ) and several chemotherapy regimens, h/o bilateral PEs, HTN, DM II who presents with confusion, hypercalcemia, hyperglycemia. He went to clinic today for treatment and related feeling weak and confused when he woke up this morning. Before this, he was feeling well and denies any fevers, chills, night sweats, head aches, visual disturbances, chest pain, new shortness of breath, cough, abdominal pain, changes in bowel movements, dysuria, lower extremity edema. He relates that he is taking his insulin as instructed and says that his blood sugars have been in the 200s consistently. He relates that since his discharge last week, he has attempted to remain very well hydrated and eat well. He says that he has taken all of his medications as instructed and denies any alcohol use. Per report, his wife stated that he has been confused intermittently and that he has been eating a large amount. She also reported that he had a blood sugar over 600 last week. In clinic, his VS were: BP: 143/95. Heart Rate: 107. O2 Saturation%: 100. Weight: 239.4 (With Clothes; With Shoes). Height: 70.5 (With Shoes). BMI: 33.9. Temperature: 98. Hospital Course: BRIEF SUMMARY Mr. is a with relapsed refractory multiple myeloma s/p autologous transplant ( ) and several chemotherapy regimens, h/o bilateral PEs, HTN, DM II who presented with malignant hypercalcemia, on CKD, hyperglycemia, and weakness. ACUTE ISSUES Malignant Hypercalcemia: Pt admitted with malignant hypercalcemia. Ca -> 10.0 ( ). Pt received pemidronate during recent admission and could not get another dose on admission because it had been less than a week since his last dose. He was treated with IV fluids and nasal calcitonin with normalization. Treatment with denosumab may be considered in the future. DM II c/b hyperglycemia: Pt has DM II and has had intermittent hyperglycemia. His glucose control is likely also impacted by IV dexamethasone that he got in clinic on . He was initially continued on his home regimen (25 U glargine QHS with ISS at meals and QHS), but required additional insulin. followed and assisted with his insulin regimen. On , he was hyperglycemic to >450. He was placed on an insulin drip for about 12 hours and then returned to SC insulin. He was instructed to check his blood sugars four times daily and to call his endocrinologist if his blood sugar is >180 PMH: PAST ONCOLOGIC HISTORY: - level bone marrow biopsy revealed 50% involvement of CD138+ plasma cells - Velcade/Dexamethasone and monthly Zometa - Pneumonia-Admitted to - Pulmonary Emboli - discontinued - secondary to Streptococcus Bovis infection - Velcade/Decadron x 1 cycle - -Once cycle of Velcade alone - - Velcade resumed - increasing on single agent Velcade (IgA 1460);dexamethsone added - cycle 13 of Velcade/Decadron - Added Revlimid at end of . Completed 3 cycles of RVD then \

It is important to address this early on in admissions; if endorsing SI at all, psych should be involved early, and a plan should be put in place to either head towards inpatient psychiatric admission for further treatment or discharge once medically stable, in order to not allow these concerns to delay appropriate discharge once his medical issues have been resolved. He is very anxious, and treatment of his anxiety appropriately can help to prevent an inappropriately prolonged admission. year old M with PMH: x HIV on ART (last CD4 ~500, VL UD), CAD s/p CABG , COPD, OSA on CPAP, PE (unprovoked) on AC, current EtoH abuse with several other comorbidities including frequent admissions for SOB & CP, admitted with SOB. Patient tells me he awoke in the middle of the night with acute onset shortness of breath while wearing CPAP. He alerted a woman at his assisted living home who called EMS. EMS reported pulse ox 90 on RA, patient was placed on NRB, currently on 2L NC O2. Patient endorses sudden onset of pleuritic chest pain while in the ED, feels like he cannot get enough air in his lungs and dry cough. H

She was also started on high flow nasal canula. She has a R groin central line placed at . On arrival to ED: - Initial vitals were: 98 111 22 117/70 98%venturi mask - She was weaned to room air - She was continued on levophed - Hospital Course: year old female with history of schizophrenia, non-verbal at baseline, presented from nursing home with acute hypoxia in setting of recently treated PNA, found to have new LLL infiltrate, ?UTI and septic shock (now resolved). Chief Complaint: dizziness Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: none Hospital Course: Information for Outpatient Providers: Mr. is a year old man h/o CAD, bicuspid aortic valve s/p AVR, atrial fibrillation, CHF and most recently redo CABG/mitral valve replacement/ who presented with acute onset, intermittent vertigo. Neurologic exam was unremarkable expect for past pointing. His exam was suggestive of left peripheral vestibulopathy but given his vascular risk factors, patient underwent MRI which did not show any evidence of acute stroke. His history and examination were most consistent with benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. With time and fluids as well as Epley maneuver, patient improved. Patient was evaluated by and was able to ambulate without difficulty. did not recommend any services at home. Otherwise, although his MRI did not show any evidence of acute stroke, it did show evidence of microhemorrages, some of which were present on previous MRIs. The microbleeds raises concern for the possibility of cerebral amyloid angiopathy. The exact risk of lobar hemorrhage on therapeutic anticoagulation in the setting of CAA is not known but it is higher than those who are not anticoagulated. Given that patient has mechanical valve and risk of thrombosis is quite high, PMH: Problems (Last Verified by , RN): AORTIC VALVE REPLACEMENT/AORTIC REGURG ASTHMA ATRIAL FIBRILLATION CAD--BYPASS GRAFT COUMEDIN GOAL IS 2.5-3.5 COLONOSCOPY , NORMAL HYPERLIPIDEMIA BACK PAIN SHOULDER PAIN ELEVATED PSA PROSTATE CANCER COUMADIN CONTRACT HEALTH MAINTENANCE HEMATOCHEZIA HEMORRHOIDS COLONIC ADENOMA CHRONIC DISEASE MANAGEMENT ADVANCE CARE PLANNING

Chief Complaint: Metastatic melanoma Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: left axillary lymphadenectomy, resection left cervical node. HPI: Mr. is an old with history of recurrent metastatic melanoma who presents for left axillary lymphadenectomy, resection left cervical node. His oncologic history dates back to , where he underwent a shave biopsy of an abdominal lesion consistent with melanoma Level IV. He also underwent wide resection in . Pathology was consistent with radial growth melanoma. Axillary sentinel node negative for melanoma. He also underwent excision of left shoulder lesion, which was negative for malignancy.In he underwent multiple excisions of small skin lesions, none consistent with melanoma. He continued to have surveillance with his local dermatologist from . More recently, Mr. in noticed an unintentional weight loss of ~40-50 lbs over the past year. His PCP obtained CT which showed a bulky left axillary and supraclavicular adenopathy, as well as likely multiple live hemangiomas. He was referred to and seen by Dr. . On he underwent PET-CT FDG-avid left axillary adenopathy and level IV cervical node. Liver lesions without FDG-avidity. Hypermetabolic thyroid gland.On he underwent a biopsy of left axillary lymph node revealed path and IHC consistent with melanoma. BRAF mutation status testing sent. Fl Hospital Course: with recurrent metastatic melanoma to left axilla, now s/p left axillary lymphadenectomy, resection left cervical node. The procedure was without complications. He was admitted overnight to the surgical ward for observation and hospital course was stable. Postoperatively, he had good pain control and was transitioned to oral pain medications. His diet was advanced as tolerated and fluids were discontinued. Postoperatively he voided and was given Flomax for PVR 300; thereafter his urination improved. His surgical site dressings remained intact without any signs of infection; JP drain was exuding acceptable amounts of serous sanguineous drainage. Patient was discharged home on POD 1,with for JP drain care and will follow-up with Dr. in clinic. Physical Exam: General: Alert, oriented,no acute distress Cardiac: regular rate rhythm Pulmonary: clear Abdomen: soft, NT/ND Incision: c/d/I, JP drain serosanguineous Extremities: warm well perfused, no edema

Original — ICD: S72.201
Chief Complaint: Left periprosthetic femur fracture Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: ORIF Left periprosthetic femur fracture with plate HPI: Mr. is a gentleman with history of CAD (s/p CABG), bilateral pulmonary emboli (on warfarin), and left total hip arthroplasty , who presented to the ED as a transfer from for a left periprosthetic distal femur fracture. Mr. reports sliding on his linoelum floor at home, resulting in his left leg "folding" behind his right with an audible crack. The injury reportedly occurred around 2:00 pm on . He had immediate onset of pain in the left thigh and was unable to stand or ambulate. He denies head strike and loss of conciousness. Hospital Course: The patient presented to the emergency department and was evaluated by the orthopedic surgery team. The patient was found to have left periprosthetic femur fracture and was admitted to the orthopedic surgery service. The patient was taken to the operating room on for ORIF Left periprosthetic femur fracture with plate, which the patient tolerated well. For full details of the procedure please see the separately dictated operative report. The patient was taken from the OR to the PACU in stable condition and after satisfactory recovery from anesthesia was transferred to the floor. The patient was initially given IV fluids and IV pain medications, and progressed to a regular diet and oral medications by POD 1. The patient was given antibiotics and anticoagulation per routine. The patient's home medications were continued throughout this hospitalization. The patient worked with who determined that discharge to rehab was appropriate. The hospital course was otherwise unremarkable. At the time of discharge the patient's pain was well controlled with oral medications, incisions were clean/dry/intact, and the patient was voiding/moving bowels spontaneously. The patient is NVI distally with PMH: - Pulmonary Emboli - Coronary artery disease, non-STEMI (post-op hip replacement) - Left foot drop and neuropathy secondary to post-op left hematoma causing nerve compression - Bilateral Pulmonary Embolisms - Umbilical hernia - Hydrocele - Speech impediment - Childhood asthma Past Surgical History: - s/p Left hip replacement (5 previous surgeries to L hip) with multiple complications. - s/p Left knee arthroscopy

Chief Complaint: Cough Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Right thoracotomy with tracheobronchoplasty using polypropylene mesh, bronchoscopy with lavage. HPI: Ms. is a yo female, former 10 py smoker (quit . Has had a chronic cough for the past years. Has had a negative methacholine challenge test in the past. Has had negative allergy testing and an unremarkable upper endoscopy. No improvement in symptoms with acid suppression. Had a bronchoscopy on , which showed severe malacia at the distal trachea, LMSB, and BI. Did well with the stent evaluation in . Subsequently had GI testing and an ENT workup. Esophageal manometry was unremarkable. BRAVO revealed score of 11.8 (normal). ENT evaluation showed muscle tension in vocal cords- recommendation was for voice therapy. Today, pt reports that her cough persists. She is having a particularly bad coughing day today. Denies recent respiratory infections. Has some dyspnea with activity. Plans on pursuing voice therapy after the surgery. Hospital Course: Ms was admitted to the Thoracic Surgery service following tracheobronchoplasty on . She tolerated the procedure well and was brought to the SICU for post-op airway monitoring. For details of the operation, please see surgeon's operative note. Her pain was managed with an epidural, which was capped and then removed on . She also received toradol, lidocaine patch, and Ativan. Her Foley was removed after her epidural was removed and she voided spontaneously. Her respiratory status was monitored closely. She was transferred to the surgical floor on . She was weaned to room air and saturated well. her diet was advanced slowly until she was on a regular diet. She tolerated this well. By , she was ambulating independently, tolerating a regular diet, saturating well on RA, and voiding spontaneously with pain well controlled. She was therefore medically ready for discharge. PMH: Mild asthma with chronic cough Memory loss Migraine Fibromyalgia B12 deficiency, anemia Gluten intolerance Osteopenia Allergic rhinitis s/p L leg neuro repair s/p scar tissue removal R ankle s/p scar tissue removal R wrist s/p tonsillectomy

Hospital Course: The patient presented to the emergency department and was evaluated by the orthopedic surgery team. The patient was taken to the operating room on for open reduction and internal fixation of her left distal tibia fracture, which the patient tolerated well. For full details of the procedure please see the separately dictated operative report. The patient was taken from the OR to the PACU in stable condition and after satisfactory recovery from anesthesia was transferred to the floor. The patient was initially given IV fluids and IV pain medications, and progressed to a regular diet and oral medications by POD 1. The patient was given antibiotics and anticoagulation per routine. The patient's home medications were continued throughout this hospitalization. The patient worked with who determined that discharge home was appropriate. The hospital course was otherwise unremarkable. At the time of discharge the patient's pain was well controlled with oral medications, incisions were clean/dry/intact, and the patient was voiding/moving bowels spontaneously. HPI: Ms. returns to clinic today. Her orthopedic history is well documented. She has known tricompartmental osteoarthritis of both knees. She presents today with ongoing right knee pain. She states that she walks times a day to walk her dog and though she is not limping when she walks, she has pain. Previous cortisone injections to the right knee helped alleviate her pain. Unfortunately, her right knee pain has returned. Hospital Course: The patient was admitted to the Orthopaedic surgery service and was taken to the operating room for above described procedure. Please see separately dictated operative report for details. The surgery was uncomplicated and the patient tolerated the procedure well. Patient received perioperative IV antibiotics. Postoperative course was remarkable for the following: Patient developed asymptomatic bradycardia on postoperative day 0. An EKG was obtained, which revealed sinus bradycardia. A troponin was sent, which returned negative. No further work-up indicated. The rest of her hospitalization was unremarkable. Otherwise, pain was controlled with a combination of IV and oral pain medications. The patient received Aspirin 81 mg twice daily for DVT prophylaxis starting on the morning of POD 1. The surgical dressing will remain on until POD 7 after surgery. The patient was seen daily by physical therapy. Physical Exam: Well appearing in no acute distress Afebrile with stable
