Chief Complaint: BOO/LUTS, anal and penile condyloma Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Dr. : Robotic-assisted suprapubic simple prostatectomy. Dr. : Microscopically assisted transanal laser destruction of anal dysplasia and laser destruction of penile dysplasia. HPI: This is a year old male with a history of BPH and urinary retention. He developed urinary retention following anal surgery and was seen for a voiding trial on He was started on doxazosin, but then developed urinary retention again the following day and presented to the where he had another foley placed. He returned to the clinic on and had another successful voiding trial that time. His Doxazosin was increased to 2 mg twice daily. Developed another episode of urinary retention later that night. Due to recurrent episodes of retention, expedited workup including a urodynamic study was performed. UDS revealed normal capacity, normal compliance, evidence of bladder outlet obstruction and bladder overactivity. Due to multiple episodes of retention and evidence of BOO he presents for surgical intervention. He also has a history of penile and anal condyloma. discussed surgical treatment options Hospital Course: Mr. was admitted to the Urology Service after undergoing the listed procedures with urology and general surgery. No concerning intra-operative events occurred; please see dictated operative note for full details. The patient received antibiotic prophylaxis. At the end of the procedure the patient was extubated and transported to the PACU for further recovery before being transferred to the floor. He was transferred from the PACU in stable condition. On POD0, pain was well controlled on PCA, hydrated with intravenous fluids for urine output >30cc/hour, provided with pneumoboots and incentive spirometry for prophylaxis, and on continuous bladder irrigation. Mr. home medications, as appropriate, were resumed and over the next several days, he was gradually titrated off the CBI. Basic metabolic panel and complete blood count were checked, pain control was transitioned to oral analgesics, diet was gradually advanced as tolerated and with further ambulation and once off CBI, the drain was removed. Foley catheter care and leg bag teaching was provided by nursing as well as self-flushing (hand irrigation) instructions. He was set up with home services. The remainder of the hospital course Physical Exam: WDWN, NAD, AVSS Abdomen soft, non-distended, appropriately tender along incision sites Incisions C/D/I drain has been removed. Foley in place, secured to medial thigh. Dr. : Microscopically assisted transanal laser destruction of anal dysplasia and laser destruction of Peyronie's disease. HPI: This is a year old male with a history of BPH and urinary retention. He developed urinary retention following anal surgery and was seen for a voiding trial on He was started on doxazosin, but then developed urinary retention again the following day and presented to the where he had another foley placed. He returned to the clinic on and had another successful voiding trial that time. His Doxazosin was increased to 2 mg twice daily. Developed another episode of urinary retention later that night. Due to recurrent episodes of retention, expedited workup including a urodynamic study was performed. UDS revealed normal capacity, normal compliance, evidence of bladder outlet obstruction and bladder overactivity. Due to multiple episodes of retention and evidence of BOO he presents for surgical intervention. He also has a history of penile and anal condyloma. discussed surgical treatment options Hospital Course: Mr. was admitted to the Urology Service after undergoing the listed procedures with urology and general surgery. No concerning intra-operative events occurred; please see dictated operative note for full details. The patient received antibiotic prophylaxis. At the end of the procedure the patient was extubated and transported to the PACU for further recovery before being transferred to the floor. He was transferred from the PACU in stable condition. On POD0, pain was well controlled on PCA, hydrated with intravenous fluids for urine output >30cc/hour, provided with pneumoboots and incentive spirometry for prophylaxis, and on continuous bladder irrigation. Mr. home medications, as appropriate, were resumed and over the next several days, he was gradually titrated off the CBI. Basic metabolic panel and complete blood count were checked, pain control was transitioned to oral analgesics, diet was gradually advanced as tolerated and with further ambulation and once off CBI, the drain was removed. Foley catheter care and leg bag teaching was provided by nursing as well as self-flushing (hand irrigation) Urinary catheterization. He was set up with home services. The remainder of the hospital course Physical Exam: WDWN, NAD, AVSS Abdomen soft, non-distended, appropriately tender along incision sites Incisions C/D/I drain has been removed. Foley in place, secured to medial thigh. Chief Complaint: abd distention Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: none HPI: w untreated HTN p/w abd discomfort. Pt noticed about 5 weeks of bloating and chronic R sided abdominal discomfort. Saw a nutritionist, who put him on a low carb diet and started on probiotics. Over the last 3 weeks he has had RUQ pain, and more recently has had constipation. He has lost 10 lbs over this time. He denies HA, confusion, weakness, numbness, aphasia, facial droop, sore throat, rhinorrhea, cough, chest pain, SOB, diarrhea, jaundice, icterus, dark urine, dysuria, urgency (though does have baseline hesitancy), joint pains, rashes. No bleeding, epistaxis, hemoptysis, melena/hematochezia, hematuria, arthritis. Had dental extractions in the last few months with only minor excess bleeding. Noticed a bruise under his R eye today and a few weeks ago noticed that a blood pressure cuff caused some bruising, which he has had a few times in the years past. No fevers, though felt slightly warm on , resolved on its own. No night sweats. Never had a colonoscopy. Saw his PCP today who sent him to ED for Hospital Course: ASSESSMENT & PLAN: h/o HTN admitted with weight loss, abd discomfort - OSH Abd/pelvic CT with L perinephric mass, mult liver hypodensities, dilated pancreatic duct - c/f metastatic disease. Also with severe thrombocytopenia. L perinephric mass, pancreatic mass with dilated PD, paraaortic , mult liver hypoattenuating lesions: These were findings identified on an OSH CT scan. There was evidence for both low grade lymphoma and pancreatic CA with likely mets to liver - although tissue pathology was not finalized on the day of the discharge. Heme/Onc was consulted during this hospitalization and the thought was that the lymphoma was present initially and then due to its associated immune dysregulation, spawned the ITP and eventual pancreatic cancer. To confirm the diagnosis of lymphoma, Mr. underwent a CT guided biopsy of the left perirenal mass. The plts had to be corrected (see below) prior to this biopsy. This presumed lymphoma is believed to be low-grade: with nl LDH, mildly elevated IgM and beta-macroglobulin levels. SPEP was normal. He will be followed by Dr. as an outpt. The history was obtained from his family, who is , as the patient is non verbal. His family reports that since 3 days ago, he has had a rash on his right neck which now appears more prominent. He seems nauseated this morning. He has not been using his neck as much as normal. He is nonverbal at baseline. No fevers per family. He has otherwise been acting like himself. His family is unsure if he has had chicken pox before. In the ED, initial vitals were: T97.2, HR 74, BP 82/43, RR 16, SpO2 98% RA. Later spiked a fever to 102.1 while being observed overnight. - Exam notable for: rash on the right neck and shoulder - Hospital Course: SUMMARY: year old man non-verbal man with Down's Syndrome, VSD s/p repair and hypothyroidism presenting with acute painful vesicular rash consistent with localized herpes zoster. ACUTE ISSUES: Herpes Zoster: Patient presented with vesicular rash most consistent with zoster. Appears to involve more than one dermatome but does not cross midline and no evidence of dissemination of superinfection. Patient was started on valacyclovir 1g q8h for 70day course (last day . Fever: patient febrile to 102.1F in the ED. Thought to be likely related to herpes zoster infection. An extensive infectious work-up (UA, CXR, CT neck, CT abd/pelvis) was pursued which was unremarkable. Patient was monitored overnight with no further fevers. Hypotension: patient found to have relatively low BPs in the ED (82-112/43-61). Recorded outpatient BPs in the , so this is not far from his baseline. Likely due to dehydration in the setting of illness as evidenced by lactate 3.1 on arrival which resolved after 3L IV fluid. Dysphagia: continued home diet of soft, ground moist foods, and pureed solids with thin liquids. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: - Complete 7-day course of valacyclovir 1gm q8h (last day - CT on showed no ma PMH: - Down's syndrome - Dysphagia (on pureed solids, ground/moist foods, and thin liquids - VSD s/p repair with Gore-Tex patch - 1+ TR - Seborrheic dermatitis - Hypothyroidism

Chief Complaint: Intraventricular hemorrhage Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: External ventricular drain HPI: Mr. is an year old man with history significant for intraparenchymal hemorrhage while on warfarin, atrial fibrillation with DDD pacemaker currently on apixaban who is transferred from outside hospital with intraventricular bleed. Per her daughter, patient was in usual state of health until morning of when he awoke at 4AM to use the urinal. He was seen to "slump over" and said he had a headache. EMS was called and he was taken to OSH where he was found to have a large intraventricular hemorrhage. He received Kcentra, levetiracetam (Keppra), was sedated and intubated and flown to . Hospital Course: Intraventricular Hemorrhage Upon arrival to , patient was sedated and intubated. Repeat non-contrast head CT showed increase in size of intraventricular hemorrhage and leftward shift. After discussion w/ family upon admission, agreed for aggressive measures. EVD was placed and repeat non-contrast head CT was performed confirming correct placement. Serial non-contrast head CT next day shows stable hemorrhage. Apixaban and anti-platelet medications were held. LMWH levels on were 0.29. He was initiated on intrathecal tPA at 2mg BID on . His repeat CT showed interval worsening in MLS and mass effect. The tPA was stopped. His family decided to make him CMO on at 13:00pm. He was extubated at 13:15pm. He passed away at 15:20pm. Atrial fibrillation/Atrial Flutter s/p DDD pacemaker Noted to have intermittent episodes of rapid ventricular rate. Heart rates were controlled with metoprolol and diltiazem. Hypertension: Systolic blood pressures controlled with hydralazine and nicardipine as needed with target less than 160. Pulmonary Ventilator dependent respiratory failure. FEN: Received enteral nutrition. Received famotidine for stress ulcer prophylaxis. Fevers: treated for UTI with ceftriaxon PMH: Squamous cell lung cancer s/p resection Basal cell cancer on nose s/p resection Cecal adenoma s/p resection Benign prostate hyperplasia Subdural hematoma Intraparenchymal hemorrhage Atrial fibrillation, paroxysmal, and atrial fluter on apixaban with DDD pacemaker placed in Hypertension Legally blind in R eye Physical Exam: General: No eye opening off propofol HEENT: Pupils asymmetric Neck: Supple, trachea midline CV: S1>S2, pacemaker Lungs: Dim at bases Abdomen: Abdomen soft, OGT in place GU: Deferred, foley in place Neuro: MS- Unresponsive, does not follow any commands or attenuate to speaker off sedation CN- Pupils asymmetric, R > L, non reactive - sluggishly . Positive corneals, cough/ gag. No obvious facial droop Sensory/Motor- No commands. Withdraws in lowers to noxious. RUE withdraws to noxious, triple flexion LUE. She describes several weeks of progressively worsening chest pressure and shortness of breath. Her chest pressure is substernal and does not radiate. These symptoms are worsened with minimal exertion such as walking short distances and even felt short of breath with removing garments in the ED. Symptoms improve with rest. These symptoms have been worsening over the last several weeks and noticed a steep decline in the last week. She also has associated presyncope/lightheadedness and queasiness. She initially went to her PCP and was sent to the ED for further evaluation. She denies any bloody or jet black stools. She has not had any vaginal bleeding; status post-hysterectomy. She denies orthopnea, PND, or worsening peripheral edema. Of note, patient states she developed similar symptoms in at that time was noted to be profoundly anemic. She states her symptoms improved greatly after receiving a transfusion. Per chart review, was admitted to in for symptomatic anemia with dyspnea on exertion and palpitations. She had an EG Hospital Course: Outpatient Providers: TRANSITIONAL ISSUES [] New medications: aspirin and sodium bicarbonate [] Changed medications: none [] Discontinued medications: none [] Has ongoing severe iron def anemia that is probably contributing to her symptoms (DOE) will likely need IV iron repletion as outpatient. Chief Complaint: "I'm ready to go." Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: none HPI: This patient is a year old woman with a history of bipolar disorder who was brought to the ED from outpatient office at on a for disorganized, erratic behavior while at a clinic appointment for her son. Her child is now in custody. Upon arrival to the unit, patient was irritable and minimally cooperative with interview. She perseverates on leaving the hospital, saying "I don't need to be here. Nobody here knows what they're talking about. The social worker sectioned me. She lied. I want to sign, I want to sign to leave." She is difficult to redirect, and is dismissive of most questions. When asked why she was sent to the hospital, she says "I'm not going to answer that." Although she endorses feeling fatigued, patient stands up in exam room and refuses to sit. She says she needs to leave the hospital by tomorrow because she has an appointment on morning, as well as a meeting on morning "with everybody, for my son". When asked what happened at today, patient says "she doesn't know what she's talking about. I'm fine." Patient denies suicidal ideation and denies depressed mood. She also denies HI and AVH. PMH: Past psychiatric history (from ED note dated by Dr. : "Patient states she has history of diagnosis of bipolar disorder. States she has several past hospitalizations, for "depression and mania". Recently, she has been on lithium but switch to Depakote due to feelings of emotional numbness, with Depakote began to have irregular periods so as of 2 days ago she switched to Tegretol, which she says she has done well on in the past. Also currently taking lorazepam and Seroquel at night, with past trials of several other antipsychotics. She denies any history of suicide attempts or self injury. Her p Physical Exam: VS: 98.0 115/86 73 17 96 General: NAD, thin-appearing woman HEENT: PERRL, MMM, OP clear, tongue w/patchy yellow-white plaques Neck: Supple. No adenopathy. Lungs: CTAB; no crackles or wheezes. CV: RRR; no m/r/g Abdomen: Soft, NT, ND. +BS Extremities: No clubbing, cyanosis, or edema. Skin: Warm and dry, sparse papular rash across back and abdomen, improved from previous exams NEUROLOGICAL EXAM: CN: PERRL, EOMI , sensation intact and symmetric V1/V2/V3, smile symmetric, shoulder shrug intact, tongue midline, no atrophy Deep tendon Reflexes: Patellar 2+ b/l Sensation: to light touch intact in all

Chief Complaint: "Sadness." Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: None HPI: This is a year old woman with a history of depression and ETOH use, who presented intoxicated and reporting SI. History difficult to obtain due to mildly slurred speech and very slow, vague responses to questions at this time. Her ETOH level on arrival was 347 at 2:05AM, seen by this examiner at 5:15AM. She states came into the hospital because of "sadness" for years, though worse over the past few weeks. Can't describe a definitive stressor that had been making things worse initially. Over the last few days she states it has been hard to "exist". She lives in an apartment alone in , getting financial support from her parents, moved to 1.5 months ago from , reports that she was raped a few months ago by a friend and this was one of the reasons she moved. She states she doesn't have close friends or supports in the area, in process of getting a job at a coffee shop nearby. She had been drinking "a lot" of vodka daily (cannot tell me exact amount at this time). While intoxicated, states she had been texting multiple friends and eventually called her sister who lives in for help, has difficulty remembering exactly what she told them but admits may have been related to suicidal thought Hospital Course: HOSPITAL COURSE SECTION OF DISCHARGE SUMMARY 1. LEGAL & SAFETY: On admission, the patient signed a and signed a CV on the next day. She was on q15 and green sharps throughout, with good behavior on the milieu. 2. PSYCHIATRIC: ) Major Depressive Disorder vs. Substance-Induced Mood Disorder: Given her history of chronic severe anxiety since childhood and depressive episodes and passive suicidality since early adolescence, she likely has MDD as indicated by her anhedonia, trouble with concentration, loss of appetite, low mood, suicidal ideation and prior attempts, sleep disturbances, and loss of interest in her usual passtimes which have lasted for significant periods of time throughout her life. She has hx of lacking response from several antidepressants. She was continued on Venlafaxine 150mg QHS which she finds moderately helpful. In context of anxiety and possible Bipolar diathesis, we started lamotrigine 25mg QHS. She found the venlafaxine and lamotrigine moderately helpful. At the time of discharge, she felt that her mood was brighter and her affect was congruently so. She remained affectively anxious but subjectively rated her anxiety . ) Post Traumatic Stress Disorder: Due to PMH: PAST PSYCHIATRIC HISTORY: Dx: depression, "shades of ADD", ETOH use. Hospitalizations: none Current treaters and treatment: has a psychiatrist in , states doesn't remember name but hates this person, looking for a new therapist Medication and ECT trials: Prozac, venlafaxine. Self-injury: last . states she threw self down a stairwell (intent was "kind of" to kill self), past cutting- not sure if intent to kill self, states had previous overdose but not going into specifics about what she took

Chief Complaint: Colon cancer Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Open Sigmoid Colectomy HPI: Per Clinic Note: Mr. is a male with a history of CAD status post MI and stent placement (on ASA/Plavix), invasive bladder carcinoma status post radical cystoprostatectomy and neobladder creation, AAA status post open repair now presents following colonoscopy with findings of a bleeding sigmoid mass. Briefly, the patient reports onset of rectal bleeding in of this year prompting a colonoscopy that was concerning for a narrowed friable area of sigmoid colon, though this was unable to be adequately visualized during the procedure. He subsequently underwent CT colonoscopy that demonstrated an area of sigmoid wall thickening in the region of concern in . He underwent a second attempt at colonoscopy in for these findings, and biopsies of the area of interest were negative for any evidence of malignancy on final pathologic evaluation. He also underwent EUS at the same time that did not demonstrate any notable abnormalities throughout the sigmoid colon. He subsequently underwent repeat CT Hospital Course: Mr. presented to holding at on for an open sigmoid colectomy. He tolerated the procedure well without complications (Please see operative note for further details). After a brief and uneventful stay in the PACU, the patient was transferred to the floor for further post-operative management. Neuro: The patient experienced severe post operative pain despite a dilaudid PCA, the dilaudid was switched to morphine which helped control the patient's pain. Once tolerating a regular diet, the patient's pain was well controlled on Tylenol and oxycodone for breakthrough pain. CV: Given the patient's history of significant cardiac disease, he was placed on continuous cardiac monitoring. He experienced bradycardia to the 30's while he was sleeping with ectopy. Chief Complaint: Shortness of breath Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Chest Tube Placement HPI: Mr. is a year old male who presented to the emergency department with symptoms of SOB and chest pain. He first noticed left upper back pain two days ago. The pain slowly progressed and at the time of the presentation to the ED he reported that the chest pain had migrated the front of his chest. He also complains of shortness of breath that he first noticed yesterday and which has progressed today during the day. Of notice, yesterday night he travelled by airplane from to to visit family. He denies any previous episodes of pneumothorax or any trauma that can have resulted in this presentation. On review of symptoms he notices that today he has experienced headaches, nausea and three episodes of vomit. He reports that he had nasal congestion and a cough few days before the back pain and SOB started. Hospital Course: Mr presented to the ED at on due to shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain and was found to have a spontaneous pneumothorax. A pigtail was placed in the ED and it was placed to -20 suction overnight. The next day the tube was placed to water seal and the X-ray showed resolution of the pneumothorax. The tube was then removed and post-pull X-ray confirmed that there was no evidence of pneumothorax. Chief Complaint: TBI s/p motorcycle collision Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: : Emergent left craniectomy for subdural hematoma evacuation and decompression : Washout of bilateral leg wounds : PEG tube placement : Left cranioplasty HPI: Eu Critical is a speaking year old male who presents to on with a mild TBI. The patient transferred to from following a motorcycle collision. The patient was the motorcycle operator, wearing a helmet, was reportedly hit by a motor vehicle at suspected high speed. His initial at revealed a subdural hematoma in addition to bilateral tibia fractures and lung contusions. He was transferred to for further management and care via MedFlight. Hospital Course: TBI skull fractures with SDH, SAH, IPH, EDH, cerebral edema Patient was transferred via MedFlight from s/p helmeted motorcycle collision with TBI. GCS at the scene was 15. Upon arrival to ED was 13. A repeat NCHCT showed expanding bleed and concern for epidural hematoma. He became more somnolent with new onset bradycardia and 1 episode of vomiting. Patient was intubated and brought to the OR for emergent craniectomy for decompression and evacuation of the left subdural/epidural hematoma. A JP drain was placed. Please see separately dictated operative report for complete details of the procedure. After surgery the patient was admitted to the trauma surgical ICU on the ACS service for management of his poly trauma. Post-op head CT showed good decompression but increased frontal and temporal contusions and the patient was closely monitored. He was given mannitol for cerebral edema which was weaned to off on . The patient was given a helmet to wear out of bed. JP drain was pulled without complication. The patient was transferred to the neurosurgery service on for ongoing management of his TBI and his other injuries were stable. Hospital Course: TBI skull fractures with SDH, SAH, IPH, EDH, cerebral edema Patient was transferred via MedFlight from s/p helmeted motorcycle collision with TBI. GCS at the scene was 15. Upon arrival to ED was 13. A repeat NCHCT showed expanding intracranial hemorrhage and concern for epidural hematoma. He became more somnolent with new onset bradycardia and 1 episode of vomiting. Patient was intubated and brought to the OR for emergent craniectomy for decompression and evacuation of the left subdural/epidural hematoma. A JP drain was placed. Please see separately dictated operative report for complete details of the procedure. After surgery the patient was admitted to the critical illness surgical ICU on the ACS service for management of his poly trauma. Post-op head CT showed good decompression but increased frontal and temporal contusions and the patient was closely monitored. He was given mannitol for cerebral edema which was weaned to off on . The patient was given a helmet to wear out of bed. JP drain was pulled without complication. The patient was transferred to the neurosurgery service on for ongoing management of his TBI and his other injuries were stable. Chief Complaint: cesarean scar pregnancy Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Tranvaginal US Guided Injection of Methotrexate HPI: yo G4P2 with history of cesarean pregnancy transferred to ED from for management of recurrent ectopic pregnancy. Patient has known she's been pregnant since last with home pregnancy test. Pregnancy confirmed that same day at , where she also had a TVUS, but was not told results, was told to follow-up as an outpatient. Patient developed vaginal bleeding today for the first time. Presented to where she was found to have a cesarean ectopic pregnancy and transferred to for further management. On arrival, denies abdominal and vaginal pain. Received IV Tylenol for headache, now resolved. VB was light, now resolved. This was a planned and desired pregnancy. She is confused as to why this is happening again and wants to know how she can avoid it in next pregnancy. Hospital Course: Ms. is a year old G4P2 with history of cesarean pregnancy 8 months prior who was transferred to from for management of cesarean scar pregnancy at approximately 6 weeks gestational age (by sure LMP . On presentation, she was hemodynamically stable without vaginal bleeding or other evidence of cesarian scare rupture or spontaneous abortion. Hematocrit was stable. A transvaginal ultrasound demonstrated a gestational sac in the lower anterior quadrant of the uterus consistent with a cesarean scare ectopic pregnancy. She was monitored on the Antepartum service overnight and remained stable throughout her stay. The patient was counseled regarding her options for termination and continuation of the pregnancy, as well as of the risks of uterine rupture, hemorrhage, and abnormal placentation. The patient was undecided, and given her clinical stability; outpatient follow-up was scheduled to further counseling and set a treatment plan. Chief Complaint: rectosigmoid cancer Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: - laparoscopic low anterior resection HPI: Mrs is a lovely yo F who was referred to our clinic for surgical consult on her rectal adeno Ca. the patient began to have changes in her bowel habits 2 month ago with the initiation of constipation and thin looking BM. she started seeing blood on TP that progress to frank blood with BM and traces of blood on a normal looking BM. she endorses having lost 10-lb for the last month and lost her appetite. she denies any abdominal pain vomiting and still has BM every day. she does report on a feeling of nausea lately. The patient was referred for colonoscopy where an endoscopicaly obstructing mass was seen in the upper rectum- Bx returned- adeno Ca. CT torso show no distal disease. The patient showed no symptoms of obstruction. Patient presenting on this admission for scheduled resection. Hospital Course: The patient was admitted to the general surgery service after undergoing scheduled laparoscopic low anterior resection for a rectosigmoid colon cancer. The procedure was uncomplicated and the patient tolerated it well (please see Operative Report for further detail). Post-operatively, she remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable throughout her entire course. Her diet was gradually advanced from clears on POD1 to a regular diet on POD2, which she tolerated without issue. She had return of bowel function on POD2. Her pain was initially well controlled on IV pain medication including a dilaudid PCA that was then transitioned to an oral regimen with adequate control by time of discharge. Her foley was removed on the morning of POD1 and she voided subsequently without issue. She ambulated independently without difficulty. She started passing some dark blood per rectum with bowel movements on POD2-3 but this was low-volume. Her hematocrit was stable and she remained hemodynamically stable. She was given instructions to return to care if she were to develop danger symptoms such as large-volume bright red blood per rectum. She was discharged home in stable condition on POD3 to follow u PMH: Her past history consistent with breast cancer that was treated with lumpectomy and radiation therapy sentinel lymph node biopsy was negative on the right breast and she is current only under surveillance. She is having occasional bronchitis due to her heavy history of smoking. She suffered from epilepsy from the age currently no symptoms at all. She has also a past history of alcoholism and she is sober for years now. The patient has rare blood type O plus w/ TYA antibody. Chief Complaint: Tracheal stenosis Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Flexible bronchoscopy with endotracheal and endobronchial biopsy HPI: Mr. is a year old male with a history of syndrome and relapsing polychrondritis which has been complicated by complex airway involvement with tracheal stenosis s/p trachestomy ( ) with multiple admissions for recurrent tracheal stenosis s/p balloon dilatation for trachea and left main stem bronchus last done (trachea up to 12 mm and the LMS bronchus up to 10 mm) who is being admitted for observation following planned flexible bronchoscopy with dilation. The patient reported for a scheduled bronchoscopy. Underwent balloon dilation of multi-level airway stenosis with bronchial wash. Received 500cc of IVF. He reports mild post-procedural pain. He denies fever, chills, chest pain or pressure, shortness of breath, abdominal pain, N/V/D edema. Hospital Course: Mr. is a year old man with a history of syndrome and relapsing polychrondritis which has been complicated by complex airway involvement with tracheal stenosis s/p trachestomy ( ) with multiple admissions for recurrent tracheal stenosis, now s/p flex bronch with repeat tracheal dilation and biopsies. ACUTE ISSUES: TRACHEAL STENOSIS SYNDROME Patient presented on for scheduled bronchoscopy, balloon dilation, and bronchial washings, which was completed without complication. The patient was admitted overnight for monitoring and remained hemodynamically stable, satting in the mid- to high-90s on 40% trach mask. He was given albuterol PRN for shortness of breath and lidocaine nebs, Tylenol, tramadol, and oxycodone for pain. Endobronchial and endotracheal biopsies were obtained during the procedure and were pending at the time of discharge. Given his stability, he was discharged home on . TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: NEW MEDS: Prednisone taper: - 50mg on on on on on [] Patient will need follow-up with Interventional Pulmonology within 4 weeks for repeat flexible bronchoscopy, which they are scheduling [] Please follow-up endobronchial and endotracheal biopsies and cytology CODE: Full (presumed) PMH: - syndrome - Relapsing polychondritis - Connective tissue disorder resulting in polychondritis and recurrent tracheal stenosis status post multiple balloon dilations, followed by rheumatology (Dr. - Nasopharyngeal stenosis following tonsillecomy/adenoidectomy - Redundant hypopharyngeal tissue - GERD - Hx pericarditis w/ pericardial stripping - Atrophic L testis & Hypoechoic lesion of R testis Physical Exam: ADMISSION EXAM: VS: 98.4 PO 123 / 70 98 20 96 40% trach GENERAL: NAD, sitting up awake and alert HEENT: AT/NC, EOMI, PERRL, anicteric sclera, pink conjunctiva, MMM NECK: supple, no LAD, no JVD HEART: RRR, S1/S2, no murmurs LUNGS: coarse rhonchi in all lung fields ABDOMEN: nondistended, nontender in all quadrants, no rebound EXTREMITIES: warm, no edema NEURO: A&Ox3, moving all 4 extremities with purpose SKIN: no rashes DISCHARGE EXAM: VS: 1444 Temp: 98.5 PO BP: 116/62 HR

Chief Complaint: Sepsis Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Intubation Dobhoff tube placement HPI: y/o male with indwelling Foley catheter (per pt's wife, for incontinence), ( ), history of AF on warfarin, nephrolithiasis, hypothyroidism, and G6PD def presents from rehab with severe sepsis i/s/o days poor Foley catheter drainage. At , during shift change, he was noticed to have more difficulty breathing and tachypnea. Wife notes that he has also endorsed right sided abdominal pain all day. No report of trauma. Hospital Course: y/o man with indwelling Foley catheter (per pt's wife, for incontinence), ( ), history of AF on warfarin, nephrolithiasis, hypothyroidism, and G6PD def presents from rehab with severe sepsis i/s/o days poor Foley catheter drainage. Septic shock: Urosepsis He presented hypotensive with elevated white count and suspected urinary source of infection. Urine grew ESBL e. coli. Stasis from obstructed foley may have played a role. CT showed bilateral hydronephrosis with bilateral renal cysts and non obstructing stones on the left. He was treated initially with meropenem and tobramycin which were narrowed to when cultures grew ESBL E. Coli. CXR showed multifocal bibiasilar opacities concerning for multifocal pneumonia, and sputum culture grew kelbsiella which was also covered by meropenem. Given obstructed foley and hydronephrosis, urology was consulted, who recommended continued outpatient follow up. He required vasorpessors on admission, which were quickly weaned. Sepsis and septic shock resolved, treated with 14 days of meropenem. Afib on warfarin with RVR: Occurred initially in ED, resolved with dilt drip. Ongoing episodes throughout hospital course- in ICU treated w/an amio load (amio PMH: -AF on Coumadin (on dig) - hypothyroidism - G6PD def - nephrolithiasis - nightly clonazepam (weaned recently over the last week) - urinary incontinence

Chief Complaint: Bicondylar left tibial plateau fracture Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: : Closed reduction and external fixation of left tibial plateau fracture HPI: p/w left knee pain and swelling s/p mechanical fall on steps of courthouse at approximately 1pm. Pt states he lost his balance and tripped, twisting his knee as he fell forward. He struck his right shoulder upon falling. No head strike or LOC. Pt reports pain in knee and inability to ambulate since time of injury. Denies any shoulder pain. No numbness or tingling of extremities. At time of evaluation, patient denies fever/chills, headache, dizziness, blurry vision, chest pain, shortness of breath, nausea/vomiting, abdominal pain, dysuria, rash. Hospital Course: The patient presented to the emergency department and was evaluated by the orthopedic surgery team. The patient was found to have left bicondylar tibial plateau fracture and was admitted to the orthopedic surgery service. The patient was taken to the operating room on for closed reduction external fixation of left bicondylar tibial plateau fracture which the patient tolerated well. For full details of the procedure please see the separately dictated operative report. The patient was taken from the OR to the PACU in stable condition and after satisfactory recovery from anesthesia was transferred to the floor. The patient was initially given IV fluids and IV pain medications, and progressed to a regular diet and oral medications by POD 1. The patient was given antibiotics and anticoagulation per routine. The patient's home medications were continued throughout this hospitalization. The patient worked with who determined that discharge to home was appropriate. The hospital course was otherwise unremarkable. At the time of discharge the patient's pain was well controlled with oral medications, incisions were clean/dry/intact, and the patient was voiding/moving bowels spontaneously. The Physical Exam: Gen: elderly male, no acute distress Neuro: alert and interactive, baseline mental status CV: palpable distal pulses bilaterally Pulm: No respiratory distress on room air LLE: in ex fix, compartments firm but compressible, SILT , Fires , no pain with passive ROM, palpable DP pulse Pertinent Results: 09:20AM BLOOD WBC-14.7 RBC-3.06 Hgb-9.1 Hct-28.4 MCV-93 MCH-29.7 MCHC-32.0 RDW-13.0 RDWSD-44.2 Plt

Sepsis due to Osteomyelitis/cellulitis/tenosynovitis He had rapid improvement with initiation of IV antibiotics and was hemodynamically stable within 12 hours of arrival to the floor. Clinical picture consistent with osteomyelitis based on fever, leukocytosis, elevated CRP, MRI, and biopsy result with Group B Streptococcus. He was evaluated by the podiatry service who recommended that he consider right hallux amputation but he was unwilling to do that, so a right hallux debridement was done and bone (with margins) sent for pathology that showed Group B Streptococcus. Original — ICD: F32.9
Chief Complaint: "A lot is happening..." Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: None HPI: Please see the initial ED consult note written by Drs. on and Dr. note on for further details. Briefly, this patient is a year old woman with a history of Bipolar disorder with psychotic features, trauma, boderline personality traits and pulmonary embolism in who self-presented to the ED for a psychiatric evaluation after she attempted suicide by trying to get hit by a speeding car. Psychiatry was consulted for a safety evaluation. Per Dr. and verified with patient, pt endoresed feelings of hopelessness and "hurting" described as "more than depression." Stated depression on and off for year, adding that she has been "irritable and paranoid." Endorsed reduced sleep, anhedonia, low energy, poor concentration, and poor appetite. She has had suicidal ideation for 1 month. She reports 2 past suicide attempts in which she cut her wrists badly enough to require surgery, year ago and years ago. She stated that on both occasions she went to the park and cut her wrist deeply with the intent to die, and she only lived when found by others. Prior to ED admission she stated that she planned to buy a razor and to kill herself by cutting her wrist, but that all the stores were closed in an area u Hospital Course: PSYCHIATRIC ) Ms. was transferred from Medicine following initiation of anti-coagulation for her pulmonary embolism. On admission to Psychiatry, she was severely depressed, with passive suicidal ideation. She had very poor insight into both her medical and psychiatric illnesses. She noted that she did not comply with anti-coagulation because she did not think her lungs were important. She also stated multiple times that she presented to to have her depression treated and not to have her psychiatric medication regimen altered. She had a very poor body image, often perseverating on her obesity; at one point she said that she thought that staff members who performed 15 minute checks were injecting her with something that "made her fat." During interviews, she had varying levels of alertness and occasionally displayed thought disorganization and blocking. Given the paranoia and disordered thought process, we suspected an element of psychosis in her presentation and increased her chlorpromazine dose to 200 mg BID. She began to show some motor disorganization which resolved after starting benztropine. To treat her depression, we started bupropion; she tolerated a low dose well so it was PMH: Past psychiatric history: - Diagnoses: Anxiety, Depression, Substance use disorder (heroin), Psychotic disorder NOS - History of assault/abuse by ex - Hospitalizations: Per Dr. note on , 4 for SIB (2 of 4 w/ concurrent SI), with recent at (discharge . Per Dr. note on - Recent psychiatric/medical course has been PE in treated at , psychiatric admission for si during which she refused anticoagulation, admitted to for medical restabilization in , transfered to inptpsych at , dischar

Chief Complaint: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: : 1. Exploratory laparoscopy. 2. Aborted radical pancreaticoduodenectomy following vascular control. 3. Celiac and common hepatic arterial lymphadenectomy for staging. 4. Retrocolic Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy after cholecystectomy. 5 HPI: Mrs. is an woman who has had two episodes of diverticulitis resulting colocolonic fistula the sigmoid colon. She had experienced increased stool frequency and presented to Dr. evaluation. A CT scan was performed mid , demonstrating slight prominence the head of the pancreas with pancreatic ductal dilatation. Subsequent MRI demonstrated a 1.8 cm lesion within the pancreatic head suspicious for a periampullary malignancy. Dr. Mrs. to Dr. performed an endoscopic ultrasound demonstrating a 2.2 cm ill-defined mass the pancreatic head. Fine-needle biopsies demonstrated adenocarcinoma with acute and chronic inflammation. The pancreatic duct was dilated to 10 mm upstream from the lesion, but the bile duct appeared normal. The ampulla also appeared normal. Mrs. recently has had abdominal bloating with increased stool frequency. Her appetite has been good. She has not had weight loss, fevers, night sweats, or new onset of diabetes. Her only complaint is of mild dyspepsia and up to 10 bowel movements per day. Hospital Course: Ms. presented to on as a same day admission for surgery. She was taken to the operating room for a planned Whipple procedure; however, intraoperative frozen section showed nodal involvement and Whipple was aborted for gastric and biliary bypass. For full details of the procedure, please see the separately dictated Operative Report. She was returned to the PACU stable condition and after satisfactory recovery from anesthesia, she was transferred to the surgical floor. She was initially kept NPO, on IV fluids, with NG tube to suction, Foley catheter and epidural for pain control. On POD1, NG tube was put to gravity and had minimal output. Patient's epidural fell out and she was started on PCA. NG was removed on POD 2 and she was advanced to a clear liquid diet which she tolerated well. Her diet was advanced as tolerated to a regular, mechanical soft diet which she tolerated well. She was transitioned to oral pain medication. evaluated the patient and recommended rehabilitation to continue recovery. On POD 6, patient was noticed to have jaundice, LFTs were elevated with T.bili 10.1. She has related medical complications, including acid reflux disease and hypertension. She develops dyspnea on exertion after minimal activity and can perhaps walk yards before she becomes short of breath. Original — ICD: M54.9
Chief Complaint: Low back pain Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: None HPI: w/ hx of HTN, hypothyroidism who presented to ED s/p 4days of atraumatic back pain x3 days. Began on upon awakening, progressively worsening, until morning when patient could not move and called EMS. Used aleve at home for pain and exercises from her chiropractor but did not improve, worsen s/p exercises. Has had a hx of lumbar subluxation, but does not see her chiropractor regularly - only when symptomatic. She called EMS and per run report she noted mid back pain x 3 days." No radiation of pain down legs. Pain awakens patient at night with any movement. Denies recent trauma, change activity, bowel/bladder incontinence, chiropractor manipulation. She denies history of nephrolithiasis, fever/chills, weight loss, dysuria. In the ED, initial vitals were: pain, Afebrile, HR 86, 117/57, 97%RA Hospital Course: w/ hx ADHD, HTN, OSA admitted for lower back pain most likely due to left lumbar muscle spasms. Acute on chronic back pain - Patient called EMS on day of admission because she could not get up from bed due to back pain x 3 days. Only red flag sign was age > , without any urinary/fecal incontinence, trauma, malignancy, weight loss, or fever. Not immunosuppressed or on steroids. Previous MRI lumbar spine in showed lumbar disk herniation and degenerative joint disease. Due to weakness to hip flexion bilaterally, MRI lumbar spine repeated, unchanged from prior without signs of cord compression. Pain most likely due to muscle spasms which limited her mobility. Pain controlled with Flexeril, Tylenol, Oxycodone and Naproxen. Patient ambulated with assistance and pain improved before discharge. Hypertension - On admission, SBP remained on low (baseline 130s). Received Received 1L IVF and improved to SBP 120s. Held home lisinopril and HCTZ while in house and held lisinopril on discharge. Depression - Continued home citalopram ADHD - Held home Adderall as nonformulary Hypothyroid - On thyroid pork (non-formulary), held while in house OSA - not using CPAP at home past due to insurance. Restar PMH: ADHD BACK PAIN DEPRESSION HYPOTHYROIDISM COLONIC ADENOMA BASAL CELL CARCINOMA

Chief Complaint: Fatigue, leukocytosis, anemia, thrombocytopenia Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Bone marrow biopsy CVL insertion Diagnostic bronchoscopy CT-Guided lung biopsy Diagnostic bronchostopy Intubated Extubated Bilateral chest tubes placed and removed Bone marrow biopsy Hospital Course: PATIENT SUMMARY: Mr. is a year-old man with a history of DM1 and asthma, with new diagnosis of AML s/p 7+3 ( ), also with concurrently diagnosed pulmonary nodules/abscesses of unknown etiology. Hospital course c/b febrile neutropenia in the setting of progressive multifocal pneumonia with BAL demonstrating Aspergillosis, initially transferred to the FICU with progression of pulmonary infection and hypoxemic respiratory failure s/p intubation. ICU course c/b volume overload/bilateral pleural effusions s/p aggressive diuresis, renal failure requiring HD now off HD with good UOP and improvement in Cr, Afib with RVR now resolved on metoprolol, hypernatremia, transaminitis likely medication-induced, and difficult to control blood glucose. Stabilized and transferred back to the floor on . Invasive aspergillosis improving by PMH: of Type 1 DM and asthma who presented to with ongoing fatigue, with further workup demonstrating new thrombocytopenia, anemia, and leukocytosis, with flow cytometry concerning for AML. The patient notes that he has had a variety of issues over the last 12 months, including increased fatigue, joint aches, tremors. He also has had increased dyspnea and was told it was asthma. Otherwise, he notes increased bruising, chills. He has been to the doctor multiple occasions for this and was treated for flu and walking pneumonia at different times earlier this year. He had residual symptoms despite trea

Chief Complaint: preterm contractions Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: none HPI: yo G2P0 at 34w6d transferred from for c/f PTL. She reports decreased fetal movement earlier this morning, therefore presented to primary OBGYN. Then developed lower pelvic cramping. On NST found to have regular contractions with SVE of . She was transferred to L&D at and made change to 2 cm. She received penicillin and BMZ at 1545. Patient then transferred to for further management. Reports worsening contractions, denies LOF. +FM. ROS: Denies fever, chills, other abdominal pain, abdominal trauma, dysuria, vaginal discharge. Hospital Course: Ms. was transferred to the Antepartum service for preterm contractions. Her initial vaginal exam was 2.5 cm dilated, and she was given a full course of betamethasone and monitored closely. Her UA, Urine culture, urine tox screen, and gonorrhea and chlamydia cultures were all negative. She was monitored with twice daily non-stress tests which were reassuring and reactive. She was seen by the NICU team. She experienced painful contractions on a few occasions during her admission, and her exam was found to be stable at 2.5cm dilation. She declined pain medications, and her contractions resolved on their own. On hospital day 3, her exam remained unchanged, and she was discharged home in stable condition with outpatient follow-up scheduled.

Chief Complaint: Right testicular mass scrotal hematoma, postoperative Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: PROCEDURE : Right radical orchiectomy PROCEDURE : EXCISION SCROTAL MASS HEMATOMA HPI: Mr. for a right testicular mass. He is a male who had just recently noted a right testicular mass. He was seen, had an ultrasound done which shows several testicular masses and he comes in for further evaluation. He denies any significant pain or discomfort. He feels that he has really not noted this mass more than a few weeks ago. He voids three to four times a day, has no nocturia. Strength of stream is normal. He denies any leakage. There is no history of hematuria, UTIs or stones. He denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, etc. Hospital Course: Mr. was admitted to Dr. service with a right testicular mass after undergoing right radical orchiectomy. No concerning intraoperative events occurred; please see dictated operative note for details. Postoperatively he developed an expanding hematoma so he was admitted for overnight observation. Chief Complaint: Left sided weakness and dysarthria Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: None Hospital Course: Mr. was admitted to the medicine floor and remained stable through his first night. The following morning, his neurologic exam improved; however he remained NPO after failing an initial speech evaluation. His home levadopa-carbidopa was restarted as a sublingual medication and his other medications were switched to IV. He was maintained on IV fluids for hydration. Subsequently transferred to Neurology service for work up of stroke. Acute Ischemic Stroke acute ischemic stroke in right frontal lobe confirmed by MRI with minor hemorrhagic conversion. No TPA given due to medical comorbidities, time (>3hours) and patients age ( ). Carotid ultrasound showed bilateral plaques and >70% stenosis bilaterally. MRA and CTA corroborated ultrasound findings. Based on this, Vascular Surgery was consulted for further management decisions. Discussed with patient's family and HCP extensively regarding risks and benefits of operative intervention, given poor functional baseline, medical comorbidities. HCP eventually decided to pursue carotid artery stenting to minimize risk of future strokes. However, given hemorrhagic conversion noted on CT, risk of bleeding from stenting was felt to be significant

She states that her cellulitis initially resolved with treatment. However, on , she started noticing small eruptions again, which she admits to scratching. She also has rash on her arms and chest, although they are without drainage. She states the rash is both itchy and painful. No fever, chills, N/V/D, myalgias, dysuria. She improved quickly with topical steroids and oral antibiotics and was discharged the next day to her rest home with close Dermatology f/u. ACTIVE ISSUES: Severe eczematous eruption: Cellulitis: Patient presented with recurrent pruritic erythematous plaques on her lower extremities. Infusion was subsequently stopped. Received IV Benadryl x1 and 100 mg hydrocortisone. Rituxan was restarted and tolerated well without additional issues. Her Hospital Course: SUMMARY STATEMENT Ms. is a female with history of high risk MDS and +WT-1 mutatation) myeloablative MUD allo HSCT on c/b GVHD of skin/eyes, recently diagnosed minimal change disease presenting with rash during rituximab infusion requiring clinical monitoring. Rituximab infusion reaction Minimal change disease: Recent diagnosis of minimal change disease , may represent GVH of kidney, most likely secondary process. IF and EM pending. Initiated rituxan therapy in outpatient clinic and developed asymptomatic skin erythema (face, forearms) lasting ~30 minutes that resolved with hydrocortisone and benadryl. Had ~20 minutes of sacral back pain during this period which resolved without intervention. Vitals remained stable, no other symptoms. Tolerated completion of infusion as inpatient with no issues requiring no additional pharmacologic intervention. Continued home prednisone, losartan. Initiated ranitidine. Patient states that she was raped today, and also reports having suicidal thoughts with plan, in setting of medication nonadherence and substance use. . On interview in the ED, Ms. reports that she was discharged about one month ago from a 15 month jail sentence for assault and battery. Since release from jail, she has been homeless though staying with friends intermittently, has been smoking crack daily, and has stopped taking all of her medications. Also states that she has been using heroin on and off. She reports that today she was raped, but wishes not to disclose any information about it and does not wish to report it. Declined SANE. . Patient states that she was raped on day of ED presentation, and also reports having suicidal thoughts with plan, in setting of medication nonadherence and substance use. On admission and during her hospital course, the patient was noted to be a reluctant and limited historian and refused to provide collateral information. . Original — ICD: C76.9
Chief Complaint: Left upper lobe lung cancer Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Left thoracotomy, left pneumonectomy, mediastinal lymph node dissection, intercostal muscle flap buttress and bronchoscopy with lavage. SUSPENSION MICROLARYNGOSCOPY, VOICE GEL INJECTION LEFT AND RIGHT VOCAL FOLD , , 22, 23, 25, 26, 27 HPI: Mr. is a current smoker with history of COPD, who was admitted for hemoptysis, and was found to have 7cm LUL mass, biopsy-confirmed squamous cell carcinoma, 10L+ on EBUS. He presented on with subacute cough, hemoptysis. CT Chest at OSH scan demonstrated 7 cm LUL mass with some obstruction of the LUL bronchus and concern for post obstructive pneumonia. He underwent Bronch/EBUS/TBNA on . Brushings of LUL mass returned cytology positive for malignant cells consistent with squamous cell carcinoma and LNs sampling of 10L + for malignancy and levels 11R,7 and 4L negative for malignancy. His obstructive PNA was treated with IV abx and then transitioned to Levaquin PO on day of discharge. Brain MRI on for staging that showed 9mm tentorial growth c/w meningioma. He was referred for surgical eval. He has had chronic DOE and cough which have not worsened recently. He has fevers, chills or nightsweats. He has lost 8 lbs since start of recent admission, but otherwise unexplained weight loss. He is able to climb two flights of stairs independently. He has a history of lung cancer in his mother who was a smoker (small cell). Hospital Course: Mr. was admitted to the hospital and taken to the Operating Room where he underwent a left thoracotomy, left pneumonectomy, mediastinal lymph node dissection, intercostal muscle flap buttress and bronchoscopy with lavage. He tolerated the procedure well and returned to the TSICU extubated and in stable condition. He maintained stable hemodynamics and his pain was controlled with an epidural. His left chest tube drained a modest amount of serosanguinous fluid and was removed on post op day 1. His epidural was eventually split for better pain control and he was able to use his incentive spirometer effectively. He had a know hypomobile left vocal cord and was evaluated by the SLP service prior to taking liquids and was cleared for nectar thick with plans for a vocal cord injection on . He was transferred to the Surgical floor and had O2 saturations of 94% on 2 liters of O2. He continued with pulmonary toilet including nebulizer treatments and his left thoracotomy site was healing well. He developed increased work of breathing and dyspnea on along with higher oxygen demands. He was transferred to the SICU for further management and required high flow oxygen therapy to maintain adequate Physical Exam: Admission Exam BP: 160/85. Heart Rate: 91. O2 Saturation%: 95. Weight: 146.7. BMI: 19.9. Temperature: 98.2. Resp. Rate: 16. Pain Score: 0. He complains of urgency, frequency, incomplete emptying, nocturia and a weak stream. He also experiences urinary incontinence and uses diapers for this. He has some constipation and firm stool; bowel movements every few days. He denies hematuria and UTIs. Hospital Course: Mr. was admitted to Dr. service after transurethral greenlight photovaporization of prostate. No concerning intraoperative events occurred; please see dictated operative note for details. Mr. received antibiotic prophylaxis and his postoperative course was uncomplicated. He received intravenous antibiotics and continuous bladder irrigation overnight. On POD1 the CBI was discontinued and he ambulated without increased hematuria. His urine was pink, clearing, and without clots. He remained a-febrile throughout his hospital stay. At discharge, the patient's pain well controlled with oral pain medications, tolerating regular diet, ambulating without assistance, and versed on foley care. He is given pyridium and oral pain medications on dischargeexplicit instructions to follow up in clinic for trial of void. Chief Complaint: "I'm tired" Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: None. HPI: Mr. is a year old man with history of poly-substance use (cocaine, alcohol, heroin) with recent relapse 1 month prior who presented to the ED on with SI with passive plan of overdosing, immediate intent. Pt was sober for 6 months prior to this relapse. He also had cough/fever and was admitted to medicine for pneumonia. Pt was started on 5 day course of levofloxacin and patient has since been medically cleared and discharged from medicine. Pt was transferred to psychiatry voluntarily. On interview, patient reports feeling very tired because he already received his trazodone and cannot tolerate extensive interview. Briefly, patient reports having increased depression x1 month and intermittent suicidal thoughts x 1 week. Pt reports thinking about overdosing on heroin. Currently denying SI and feeling safe on the unit. He reports one previous suicide attempt, less than years ago, when he tried to OD with heroin, but "came out of it". Pt also reports relapsing on substances (cocaine, alcohol, and heroin) about 1 month ago. Last use for all three substances was . Pt also reports recently becoming homeless 2 weeks ago and sleeping on a friend's couch with limited social supports. Currentl Hospital Course: ) LEGAL & SAFETY: On admission, the patient signed a conditional voluntary agreement (Section 10 & 11) and remained on that level throughout their admission. He was also placed on 15 minute checks status on admission and remained on that level of observation throughout while being unit restricted. ) PSYCHIATRIC: There were acute behavioral events over the weekend after initial arrival. He was continued on his home medications: abilify 15 mg PO daily (for history of paranoid thoughts per patient), gabapentin, increased to 400 mg PO TID, which patient found helpful for both anxiety and knee pain, as well as trazodone 25 mg PO qhs PRN insomnia. We did not feel trazodone PRN was needed at time of discharge. He was intermittently given PRN valium Q4 hrs on psychiatry floor per protocol, and this was tapered off. At time of discharge he denied further symptoms of alcohol withdrawal. Of note, per notes from past presentations to psychiatry consult service, it was not clear patient in the past had a clear primary mood or anxiety disorder, as much of previous SI had occurred in setting of substance use, in the past concerning for instrumental SI. In addition, as his condition continued to i PMH: Reviewed and updated where needed from initial psychiatry consult note by Dr. on : "

Original — ICD: D64.9
Chief Complaint: anemia Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: none HPI: Ms. is a woman with recently diagnosed cervical adenocarcinoma stage IB2 on current chemo/radiation therapy (last dose cisplatin C1D29 was who presents with malaise and dizziness. She presented for her dose of radiation today where the patient complained of feeling cold, having headaches, heart palpitations and feeling very tired. She explains that for the past 2 weeks, she has been feeling weaker and weaker. She has had about 10 migraines with aura within this time frame, which is very unusual for her. The headaches are rather classic for her, but also seem to extend down her neck and the back of her head. That area feels stiff to her and thus, causes her pain. She has also had light-headedness that has worsened. CBC drawn in clinic showed h/h of 8.2/22.7, down from 10.7/31.8 on . Thus, she was referred to the ED for further care. She denies any significant vaginal bleeding. In fact, her bleeding has significantly improved since starting treatment. She no longer has bright red blood. She has developed significant hemorrhoids from radiation and has significant discomfort from them. She has had occasional bleeding from the hemorrhoids, but has only seen the toilet bowel full of brig Hospital Course: Ms. is a woman wit recently diagnosed cervical adenocarcinoma stage IB2 on concurrent chemo/radiation therapy who presents with malaise and dizziness and found to be anemic. Anemia Likely due to cisplatin induced marrow suppression. Patient does not have any significant bleeding either from her rectum or vagina. She may be under-reporting her blood losses, but given timing of cisplatin and anticipated nadir along with her other cell line decreases, most likely due to poor production rather than GI losses. She was transfused 1 unit pRBC with imrpovement in her hematocrit/hemoglobin from 8.2 to 9.2 Headache: two phenotypes with history of migraine with aura but more currently has tension type headache. Improving with fluids and Tylenol/ibuprofen thrombocytopenia leukopenia Most likely also cisplatin-induced. Currently not neutropenic. Will continue to monitor cervical adenocarcinoma, stage IB2: On concurrent chemotherapy with cisplatin and radiation therapy. She has completed 28 days and has 2 fractions remaining. She will have brachytherapy thereafter. - f/u with outpatient oncologist Rectal pain hemorrhoids Cont home regimen of topical agents

She explains that for the past 2 weeks, she has been feeling weaker and weaker. She has had about 10 pulmonary edema with aura within this time frame, which is very unusual for her. The headaches are rather classic for her, but also seem to extend down her neck and the back of her head. That area feels stiff to her and thus, causes her pain. She has also had light-headedness that has worsened. CBC drawn in clinic showed h/h of 8.2/22.7, down from 10.7/31.8 on . Thus, she was referred to the ED for further care. She denies any significant vaginal bleeding. In fact, her epistaxis has significantly improved since starting treatment. She no longer has bright red blood. She has developed significant rectal prolapse from radiation and has significant discomfort from them. She has had occasional bleeding from the hemorrhoids, but has only seen the toilet bowel full of brig Hospital Course: Ms. is a woman wit recently diagnosed cervical adenocarcinoma stage IB2 on concurrent chemo/radiation therapy who presents with malaise and dizziness and found to be anemic. Anemia Likely due to cisplatin induced marrow suppression. Patient does not have any significant bleeding either from her anal fissure or vagina. She may be under-reporting her blood losses, but given timing of cisplatin and anticipated nadir along with her other cell line decreases, most likely due to poor production rather than GI losses. She was transfused 1 unit pRBC with imrpovement in her hematocrit/hemoglobin from 8.2 to 9.2 Headache: two phenotypes with history of irritable bowel syndrome with aura but more currently has tension type headache. Improving with fluids and Tylenol/ibuprofen thrombocytopenia leukopenia Most likely also cisplatin-induced. Currently not neutropenic. Will continue to monitor cervical adenocarcinoma, stage IB2: On concurrent chemotherapy with cisplatin and radiation therapy. She has completed 28 days and has 2 radiation dermatitis remaining. She will have brachytherapy thereafter. - f/u with outpatient oncologist Rectal pain hemorrhoids Cont home regimen of topical agents

Original — ICD: C91.0
Hospital Course: Mr. is a male with a history of CLL who presented after fall and head strike with confusion, progressive weakness, and discoordination, found to have mild hypercalcemia, a new renal mass, large leukocytosis, and hypercalcemia concerning for transformed CLL as well as newly severe AS. His course was complicated by toxic metabolic encephalopathy with possible seizure, but no epileptic forms caught on EEG. Head CT and MRI were negative for acute pathology. After family meeting with palliative care and his oncologist, it was determined he was not a candidate for chemo or other aggressive treatment due to his renal dysfunction and overall poor health; PET-CT was done on the small change his findings were due to anything other than CLL that could be treated by non-chemotherapeutic means. On , following PET-CT, he was still somnolent and had had an episode of shaking overnight, so family elected to take him home on hospice and deferred biopsy of the nodes given his ineligibility for treatment.

Chief Complaint: Right femoral neck fracture Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: : Right hip hemiarthroplasty Hospital Course: The patient presented to the emergency department and was evaluated by the orthopaedic surgery team. The patient was found to have right femoral neck fracture and was admitted to the orthopaedic surgery service. The patient was taken to the operating room on for right hip hemiarthroplasty, which the patient tolerated well. For full details of the procedure please see the separately dictated operative report. The patient was taken from the OR to the PACU in stable condition and after satisfactory recovery from anesthesia was transferred to the floor. The patient was initially given IV fluids and IV pain medications, and progressed to a regular diet and oral medications by POD 1. The patient was given antibiotics and anticoagulation per routine. The patient's home medications were continued throughout this hospitalization. The patient worked with who determined that discharge to rehab was appropriate. The hospital course was otherwise unremarkable. At the time of discharge the patient's pain was well controlled with oral medications, incisions were clean/dry/intact, and the patient was voiding/moving bowels spontaneously. The patient did endorse some minor shortness of breath. Chest PMH: significant for heart disease including A. fib not currently anticoagulated, CAD status post RCA stenting, pacemaker placement, history of TIA, and T2DM who presents in transfer from with right femoral neck fracture for definitive orthopedic care. Patient states that around 5 while standing up from the dinner table he fell reaching for his walker. He notes landing on his right side and explains immediate right hip pain. He was unable to rise. He denies head strike. He denies loss of conscious. He notes pain only to his right hip. He denies pain elsewhere. He has no numbness or tingling to the Physical Exam: Right lower Extremity - Incisional dressing c/d/i - Fires - SILT s/s/sp/dp/tn - Foot WWP Pertinent Results: See OMR

Chief Complaint: Hypoglycemia Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: N/A HPI: Mr. is a man with DMII (on insulin) c/b diabetic nephropathy s/p LRRT ( ), pAfib (on warfarin), neurogenic bladder s/p neobladder ( ) who was sent to the ED from for severe hypoglycemia and is admitted for management of recurrent hypoglycemia. The patient went to an appointment at for a scheduled wound check. During check-in vitals, the patient developed altered mental status and somnolence. A code blue was called and he was found to have a FSBG of 24. He received oral glucose and IV D50 25gm given with increase in FSBG to 220s. The patient's mental status returned to his baseline and he was transferred to the ED for management of severe hypoglycemia. Of note, the patient had a similar episode of hypoglycemia in for which he was evaluated in the ED by and subsequently sent home with outpatient follow-up. In the ED, initial vitals were: 97.6, HR102, BP175/68, RR20, 97% RA FSBG: 120 -> 45 on presentation - Exam notable for: LUNGS: expiratory wheezes at bases bilaterally ABD: suprapubic catheter in place, NDNT EXT: 2+ b/l edema, 2cm clean based ulcer on left lateral distal shin without purulence or drainage (see OMR for picture) - Hospital Course: Mr. is a year old male with history of Type II DM, complicated by diabetic nephropathy s/p LRRT ( ), ileo-neobladder ( ), dilated cardiomyopathy, paroxysmal afib on warfarin, who initially presented from clinic after code blue was called for unresponsiveness. Was found to have finger stick in the with subsequent improvement in mental status after IV dextrose administration. Hypoglycemia was ultimately attributed to incorrect administration of Humalog, where patient endorsed administered 10 units Humalog for all >100 prior to meals. Was seen by during hospitalization, lantus was decreased from 25 units QHS to 15 units QAM. Sliding scale insulin was also down-titrated and patient had stable fasting glucose and fingersticks prior to discharge. ACTIVE ISSUES: Hypoglycemia Toxic metabolic encephalopathy - Patient with type II DM, presented from clinic after code blue was called for unresponsiveness. Patient was found to have finger stick in the , received IV and oral dextrose with subsequent improvement in mental status. Was evaluated by during hospitalization. The patient was found to have a L both bone forearm fracture and was admitted to the orthopedic surgery service. The patient was taken to the operating room on for revision L both bone forearm fracture, which the patient tolerated well. He had a wound vac closure due to inability to close the skin. The patient was taken from the OR to the PACU in stable condition and after satisfactory recovery from anesthesia was transferred to the floor. The patient was initially given IV fluids and IV pain medications, and progressed to a regular diet and oral medications by POD 1. The patient was given antibiotics and anticoagulation per routine. The patient's home medications were continued throughout this hospitalization. The patient worked with who determined that discharge to home was appropriate. The hospital course was otherwise unremarkable. Original — ICD: G40.0
Chief Complaint: Seizures Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: None HPI: Mr. is a with a history of multiple embolic strokes in i/s/o endocarditis, mitral valve repair , and status epilepticus requiring 3 AEDs, which he has since stopped AMA. He presents today with 3 weeks of confusion, unsteadiness, fatigue, and panic attacks. After his GTC in he required Keppra BID, phenytoin 300 daily, and lacosamide 100 BID to control his recurrent seizures. Due to mood changes, he weaned himself off of his AEDs against medical advice, and has not taken any of his AEDs for the past 3 weeks. Initially he felt better, but over the past weeks he and his family have noticed changes in his behavior. Most notably, he reports being "foggy", confused, and unsteady on his feet. He has required assistance when walking and feels like he is going to fall forward when he closes his eyes while standing. He says he does not perceive the room spinning and does not feel lightheaded or like he is going to pass out. His gait impairment has been acutely worse in the past week. In addition to the imbalance, he reports fatigue that is throughout his "whole body". He also described seeing "suns" moving across his visual field sometimes. He also says he has had recurrent panic attacks, dur Hospital Course: Patient was admitted to the neurology service because of presentation concerning for stroke. Patient had episode of status epilepticus in and had been on phenytoin, levetiracetam, and lacosamide. Patient two to three weeks ago self-weaned himself off of his medications. During monitoring, he reported spells of seeing dots of bright lights and this rising sensation in the abdomen. Patient was monitored for two days continuously and there was generalized slowing but no recorded epileptiform activity. Patients neurologic examination throughout this hospitalization was negative except for chronic bilateral right visual field loss. Patient will be discharged with lacosamide 150 mg twice daily which is increased from previous dose of 100 mg twice daily. Patient will be discharged to acute rehabilitation facility because of deconditioning. Patient will follow up with his outpatient neurologist. PMH: Anxiety Basal Cell Carcinoma Cerebrovascular Accident, embolic Endocarditis, Strep Viridans Homonymous Hemianopsia Hyperlipidemia Mitral Regurgitation TMJ

Chief Complaint: Fever Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: None HPI: man with a history of CAD s/p PCI, bicuspid aortic valve and MV-regurgitation / prolapse who presented to the ED with fevers and cough. The patient reports that he went to his PCPs on and received the flu vaccine, thereafter he started feeling "woozy" which he attributed to getting the vaccine. A few days later he started getting a cough which he largely shrugged off as nothing but then he started getting a fever. Because of his valve history the patient usually takes Erythromycin for 3 days whenever he gets a history to prevent an infection of his heart valves. He didn't do that this time, he says "I can't explain why I didn't" but instead he called his PCP who instructed him to come in for blood cultures. He also had Hospital Course: Mr. is an man with a history of CAD s/p PCI, bicuspid aortic valve and MV-regurgitation / prolapse who presented to the ED with fevers, cough, hemoptysis, found to have multifocal pneumonia. Hospital course complicated by Afib with RVR, flash pulmonary edema and fluid overload. Acute hypoxic respiratory failure due to Flash pulmonary edema in the setting of Afib with RVR: Occurred in the setting of pneumonia and receiving 2L IVF in the ED. Received 20 mg IV Lasix and IV metop and diltiazem which improved his heart rates and hypoxia. CXR was consistent with flash pulmonary edema. He improved but remained fluid overload and requiring oxygen and was diuresed further with 20 mg IV Lasix daily, transitioned to 20 mg PO Lasix daily but then this was discontinued due to euvolemia on exam and evidence of overdiuresis with Cr up to 1.4 and BUN up to 44. For Afib with RVR, the patient was put on metoprolol for rate control but then was switched to carvedilol due to ongoing hypertension and tachycardia. After switching to carvedilol his HR improved to along with diuresis with Lasix. His SBP was between 100s-150s prior to discharge. The patient was concerned that SBP of 100 was too low for him PMH: - CAD s/p PCI x2 ( ) - HTN - Mitral valve prolapse - Aortic REgurgitation (Cardiologist - - HLD - PUD - BPH Physical Exam: ADMISSION EXAM: Vitals: 0816 Temp: 97.9 PO BP: 146/70 R Lying HR: 78 RR: 18 O2 sat: 96% O2 delivery: Ra Pain Scale: General: Patient appears overall robust especially for his age. He is sated upright in bed, there is an empty breakfast in front of him and he is fully interactive, and speaks purposefully and intelligently. Alert, oriented and in no acute distress HEENT: Sclera anicteric, MMM, oropharynx clear Neck: supple, JVP low, no LAD appreciated Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, moving air well and symmetrically, no wheezes, rales or rhonchi appreciated. Coughing up dark tan sputum

Chief Complaint: Dyspnea/ swelling Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Nasopharyngoscopy HPI: man history of CAD status post PCI, hypertension, diabetes, COPD, sabershape trachea without evidence of tracheobronchomalacia, active smoker presents with 1 week of worsening dyspnea. The patient has been hospitalized for COPD exacerbations multiple times. His most recent episode started a week ago, where he found himself short of breath even at rest. The patient says he needs to catch his breath while eating. Reports that he is short of breath while supine, though not necessarily worse. He is afraid to go to sleep, as he wakes up gasping for air. He endorses cough but no sputum production. Reports problems managing secretions, and difficulty swallowing small amounts of solids and liquids. States that he almost passed out after choking on a small amount of food recently. He reports some chest pain, which he attributes to his breathing, and reports is not pleuritic. He denies fevers, sick contacts. He was recently seen by his PCP, who put him on steroids. He also uses his Spiriva inhaler daily, along with his albuterol nebulizer, with mild improvement. He states he only intermittently takes enalapril and last took it 2 days ago after having not taken it for weeks. After this time, Hospital Course: w/ history of CAD s/p PCI, HTN, NIDDM2, COPD, sabershape trachea w/o e/o tracheobronchomalacia, active tobacco use p/w dyspnea likely d/t COPD exacerbation w/ possible contribution from angioedema in the setting of recent initiation of enalapril. He was evaluated by interventional pulmonology with bedside nasopharyngoscopy which showed no cord edema but posterior tongue edemana. Intervention was not advised and he received solumedrol and albuterol nebs. He was admitted for observation and treatment of angioedema and presumed COPD exacerbation, evaluated by speech and swallow for swallow safety, treated with steroids, antihistamines, Enalapril was stopped and amlodipine initiated for blood pressure management. ACUTE/ACTIVE ISSUES: Dyspnea: His shortness of breath was attributed to COPD exacerbation though there may have been a component of contribution from angioedema in the setting of recent ACEi (Enalapril) initiation for blood pressure management. We continued home duo-nebs and albuterol. We started burst dose steroids of prednisone at 60mg for a total course of 5 days and azithromycin for four day course. He initially required face tent at 35% and was quickly weaned to room air. PMH: - CAD, c/b prior STEMI, cath w/ patent LAD stent, LPDA CTO s/p DES, EF 45-50%, with anteroseptal and inferoseptal AK, apical HK, mild MR - HTN - HLD (intolerant to statins) - DMII - Depression/Anxiety - COPD/asthma - Diverticulitis Physical Exam: ADMISSION Exam Vitals: HR 74, BP 160/101, RR 19, Sat 99% on RA gen: no acute respiratory distress, conversant heent: eomi, perrla, trachea midline, lips mildly swollen, able to open his mouth CV: RRR pulm: coarse lung sounds GI:
